qs.q:
Railway Experiences — Which person…

A=Alec (ill, against doctor's advice, repeat trip, everything changed/same, missed adventure, got off, flew home)
B=Brooke (missed train, stayed positive, caught next, daydreamed, interviewer also late)
C=Chloe (standing in corridor, longed for home, cramped compartment, luggage, bends, nauseous)
D=Daniel (returning from London bookshops, full of foreign students, fell asleep, stranger woke him, would miss connection)
E=Ellis (packed commuter train, teenagers took seats, sick of commuting, decided to change life)
F=Francesca (born in London, returned after years abroad, underground felt strange, felt like another country)

0. had wanted to buy a book? [D=Daniel: 'returning home after a day searching the bookshops']
1. had to change trains?
2. had a lot of luggage?
3. missed their train?
4. made their journey after dark?
5. fell asleep?
6. did not have a seat?
7. was homesick?
8. did some work on their journey?
9. felt like a tourist?
10. changed their mind?
11. was on their regular journey?
12. was travel sick?
items: 8 — did some work on their journey?

pairs.l: 8 — did some work on their journey?

qs.exp: 1=D (Daniel: 'he must have thought I was one of them... good thing he woke me, because otherwise I would have missed my CONNECTION'). 2=F (Francesca: 'with my bags and suitcase WEIGHING ME DOWN'). 3=B (Brooke: 'seeing my train leave the station without me'). 4=E (Ellis: 'the window reflected the ghost-like lit-up strained faces' = noćno putovanje). 5=D (Daniel: 'I stared at my newspaper... The next thing I knew was that one of them was shaking my shoulder'). 6=E (Ellis: 'teenagers had taken up the seats'). 7=C (Chloe: 'How I longed to be back where I had come from'). 8=B (Brooke: 'catching up with my emails and dealing with the office ones'). 9=F (Francesca: 'it looked strange, like I was in another country'). 10=A (Alec: 'I began to regret my decision. So I got off the train'). 11=E (Ellis: 'I'd had enough of it, this COMMUTING'). 12=C (Chloe: 'the carriage swaying with the many bends... had made my stomach turn so much').

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"He was free to travel since he didn't have a home of his own or anything to keep him where he was. And he was a happy, well-adjusted chap. He liked to talk to the public and see them enjoy themselves."

What was his main reason for joining a circus?
A It gave him the chance to travel.
B He didn't have a home.
C He needed the money.
D He enjoyed entertaining people.
opts: It gave him the chance to travel.
qs.exp: 'He LIKED TO TALK TO THE PUBLIC and see them ENJOY THEMSELVES' — glavna motivacija bila je zabavljanje publike = D.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"He was said to stand 7ft 4in tall, and the attention he received from the press and public was his first indication that his unusual height might be a means to make a living."

He realized that he could make money out of his height…
A when he was in care.
B while he was in Canada.
C during a royal celebration.
D at Chigwell.
qs.exp: 'In a PARADE OF GIANTS as part of the CELEBRATIONS FOR THE CORONATION OF KING GEORGE V' = kraljevska proslava = C.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"'His height could be seen as a blessing,' said Jim Cook, 'because it gave him a life he could never otherwise have enjoyed.'"

How did he feel about his height?
A It did not trouble him.
B He felt he was a freak.
C He thought people laughed at him.
D He was grateful for it.
opts: He felt he was a freak.
He thought people laughed at him.
qs.exp: 'He was a HAPPY, WELL-ADJUSTED CHAP' = nije ga mučilo = A (It did not trouble him). 'Blessing' dolazi od Jim Cooka, ne izravno od Stanleya.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"'He just wanted to bring in the crowds.' Stanley claimed he was 8ft 4in and continued to do so for the rest of his life."

His manager…
A lied to him.
B exploited him.
C treated him fairly.
D treated him like a member of the family.
opts: treated him like a member of the family.
qs.exp: 'He had a good WORKING RELATIONSHIP with Don, who NEVER TOOK ADVANTAGE of him' = tretirao ga pošteno = C.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"'I'd say that its role in helping me RECONNECT WITH FAMILY has been its GREATEST GIFT to me.'"

Jim Cook is particularly appreciative of the fact that…
A he has found out about his family.
B he has had the chance to travel.
C he has received money for his work.
D he has revived the memory of his great-uncle.
opts: he has found out about his family.
he has had the chance to travel.
he has received money for his work.
he has revived the memory of his great-uncle.
qs.exp: 'Its role in HELPING ME RECONNECT WITH FAMILY has been its GREATEST GIFT to me' = pronašao obitelj = A.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"His doctor's case notes say he stood 7ft 9in tall, which is now known to have been the case."

What was Stanley Cook's true height?
A 7ft 4in.
B 7ft 9in.
C 8ft 4in.
D 8ft 11in.
qs.exp: 'His DOCTOR'S CASE NOTES say he stood 7FT 9IN, which is NOW KNOWN to have been the case' = stvarna visina = B.

qs.q:
The desire to define ourselves

"Personality fascinates and challenges us. (19) ___. Meanwhile, our identity and relation to the world is defined in the categories psychologists have identified."

A They tended to define personality purely as a potentiality to behave in a certain way.
B Aside from the satisfaction of cracking the code, the aim was to predict human behaviour.
C If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of human personality traits.
D Psychologists and scientists have devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits, many different from their parents.
F They make us the individuals that we are, but also unpredictable.
G Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave in certain situations.
H It shows that we have several personalities, depending on the situation.
opts: A — Defined personality purely as potentiality to behave in a certain way.
B — Aim was to predict human behaviour.
C — Could build a complete lexicon of personality traits.
D — Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E — A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits.
F — They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G — Each trait predicts the way you may behave.
H — We have several personalities depending on situation.
qs.exp: 'Personality fascinates and challenges us. (19)___. Meanwhile, our identity defined by psychologists.' → D: Psychologists and scientists have devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.

qs.q:
The desire to define ourselves

"In reality, we are all made up of conflicting traits. (20) ___. For example, we can be careful in one area but spontaneous thrill-seekers in another."

A They tended to define personality purely as a potentiality to behave.
B Aside from the satisfaction of cracking the code, the aim was to predict behaviour.
C If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of traits.
D Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits.
F They make us the individuals that we are, but also unpredictable.
G Each trait predicts the way you may behave.
H It shows that we have several personalities depending on situation.
opts: A — Defined personality purely as potentiality.
B — Aim was to predict behaviour.
C — Could build a complete lexicon.
D — Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding.
E — A child born with recognisable traits.
F — They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G — Each trait predicts the way you may behave.
H — We have several personalities depending on situation.
qs.exp: 'We are all made up of conflicting traits. (20)___. For example, careful in one area but spontaneous in another.' → F: They make us the individuals that we are, but also unpredictable.

qs.q:
The desire to define ourselves

"Galton proposed that the most significant personality differences were encoded in their language. (21) ___. This theory was debated and refined over the next 100 years."

A They tended to define personality purely as a potentiality to behave.
B Aside from the satisfaction of cracking the code, the aim was to predict behaviour.
C If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of human personality traits.
D Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits.
F They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G Each trait predicts the way you may behave.
H It shows that we have several personalities depending on situation.
opts: A — Defined personality purely as potentiality.
B — Aim was to predict behaviour.
C — If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of traits.
D — Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding.
E — A child born with recognisable traits.
F — They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G — Each trait predicts the way you may behave.
H — We have several personalities depending on situation.
qs.exp: 'Personality differences encoded in language. (21)___. This theory debated and refined.' → C: If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of human personality traits.

qs.q:
The desire to define ourselves

"He identified five broad traits known as 'the big five': openness, neuroticism, conscientiousness, extroversion and agreeableness. (22) ___. If, say, you register high in openness, you are likely to be emotionally adventurous."

A They tended to define personality purely as a potentiality to behave.
B Aside from the satisfaction of cracking the code, the aim was to predict behaviour.
C If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of traits.
D Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits.
F They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave in certain situations.
H It shows that we have several personalities depending on situation.
opts: A — Defined personality purely as potentiality.
B — Aim was to predict behaviour.
C — Could build a complete lexicon of traits.
D — Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding.
E — A child born with recognisable traits.
F — They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G — Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave in certain situations.
H — We have several personalities depending on situation.
qs.exp: 'Identified the big five traits. (22)___. If high in openness, you are likely to be adventurous.' → G: Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave in certain situations.

qs.q:
The desire to define ourselves

"What did researchers such as Galton and Cattell hope to gain? (23) ___. Personality is only of interest to psychologists if it can give them information about how we're likely to behave."

A They tended to define personality purely as a potentiality to behave.
B Aside from the satisfaction of cracking the code of human personality, the aim was to predict human behaviour.
C If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of traits.
D Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits.
F They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave.
H It shows that we have several personalities depending on situation.
opts: A — Defined personality purely as potentiality.
B — Aside from cracking the code, the aim was to predict human behaviour.
C — Could build a complete lexicon of traits.
D — Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding.
E — A child born with recognisable traits.
F — They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G — Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave.
H — We have several personalities depending on situation.
qs.exp: 'What did researchers hope to gain? (23)___. Personality only of interest if gives info about behaviour.' → B: Aside from the satisfaction of cracking the code, the aim was to predict human behaviour.

qs.q:
The desire to define ourselves

"Rita Carter has recently published research which argues that people behave differently depending on context. (24) ___. 'Instead of saying we're one particular type,' she says, 'it is more complex.'"

A They tended to define personality purely as a potentiality to behave.
B Aside from cracking the code, the aim was to predict behaviour.
C If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon.
D Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding.
E A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits.
F They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave.
H It shows that we have several personalities, and the one that comes to the fore depends on the situation we find ourselves in.
opts: A — Defined personality purely as potentiality.
B — Aim was to predict behaviour.
C — Could build a complete lexicon.
D — Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding.
E — A child born with recognisable traits.
F — They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G — Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave.
H — It shows that we have several personalities, and the one that comes to the fore depends on the situation.
qs.exp: 'Carter argues people behave differently depending on context. (24)___. Instead of saying one type, it is more complex.' → H: It shows that we have several personalities, and the one that comes to the fore depends on the situation.

qs.q:
Life in the City

"People in cities walk (25) ___ average at 1 to 1.5 metres per second."

A for
B by
C in
D on
qs.exp: 'Walk ON average' — fiksna kolokacija: on average = prosječno.

qs.q:
Life in the City

"For the past 30 years we (26) ___ told the hurried pace of urban life is potentially more harmful."

A are
B were
C have been
D had been
qs.exp: 'For the past 30 years we HAVE BEEN told' — present perfect za period koji traje do danas (for the past 30 years).

qs.q:
Life in the City

"We even speed up to maximise the (27) ___ of the pleasure we start experiencing."

A intensity
B strength
C force
D volume
qs.exp: 'Maximise the INTENSITY of the pleasure' — 'intensity' = intenzitet, jačina (o osjećajima/iskustvima).

qs.q:
Life in the City

"Learning to respect another person's space so as (28) ___ on their privacy."

A not intrude
B not to intrude
C not intruding
D intruding not
qs.exp: 'So as NOT TO INTRUDE on their privacy' — fiksna konstrukcija: so as to + infinitive; negacija: so as not to.

qs.q:
Life in the City

"Shopping transactions take place (29) ___ a distance of at least 1.5 metres."

A on
B at
C in
D during
qs.exp: 'Take place AT a distance' — fiksna kolokacija: at a distance = na razdaljini.

qs.q:
Life in the City

"These social rules make the beginning of a friendship with strangers more difficult, (30) ___ turns the city into a lonely place."

A which
B what
C that
D this
qs.exp: '(30)___ turns the city into a lonely place' — ne-restriktivna relativna zamjenica 'which' (uz zarez, odnosi se na cijelu prethodnu surečenicu).

qs.q:
Life in the City

"The long-term city dweller could have 1,800 social contacts; (31) ___, they end up having no more than five."

A meanwhile
B however
C moreover
D therefore
qs.exp: 'Could have 1,800 contacts; HOWEVER, end up having no more than five' — 'however' za kontrast/suprotnost.

qs.q:
Life in the City

"Enjoying city life would not be possible if the inhabitants (32) ___ by a set of strict rules."

A do not live
B will not live
C are not living
D were not living
qs.exp: 'Would not be possible if the inhabitants WERE NOT LIVING by rules' — uvjetna rečenica 2. tipa (nerealni uvjet u sadašnjosti): if + past continuous.

qs.q:
CERN

"It is an international organization (33) ___ purpose is to operate the world's largest particle physics laboratory."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Organization WHOSE purpose is to operate' — posvojni relativni prilog 'whose' (organization + its purpose = whose purpose).

qs.q:
CERN

"Twenty European countries (34) ___ part in its work."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Twenty countries TAKE part in its work' — fiksna kolokacija: take part in = sudjelovati u.

qs.q:
CERN

"The name CERN also refers (35) ___ the laboratory."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Refers TO the laboratory' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: refer to = odnositi se na.

qs.q:
CERN

"Numerous experiments have been conducted (36) ___ CERN by scientists from all over the world."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Conducted AT CERN' — prijedlog 'at' za institucije/mjesta (conducted at a laboratory/organization).

qs.q:
CERN

"It (37) ___ this data immediately available to researchers around the world."

(Upiši jednu ili dvije riječi)
qs.exp: 'It MAKES/RENDERS this data immediately available' — 'make available' ili 'render available' = staviti nešto dostupnim.

qs.q:
CERN

"CERN's researchers seem to (38) ___ found the Higgs boson."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Seem to HAVE found' — perfektni infinitiv: seem to have + past participle (za prošlu radnju).

qs.q:
CERN

"This particle was imagined and named 50 years (39) ___ by theoretical physicist Peter Higgs."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: '50 years AGO' — 'ago' za prošlu radnju mjerenu od sadašnjosti.

qs.q:
CERN

"The discovery might result (40) ___ an explanation of the way the universe was ordered after the Big Bang."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Result IN an explanation' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: result in = rezultirati nečime.

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that university students should take a job while studying. Others disagree."

Discuss arguments for and against this view and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA rad uz studij: financijska neovisnost, radno iskustvo, upravljanje vremenom, CV. PROTIV: manje vremena za učenje, pad ocjena, stres, propuštanje studentskog iskustva. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (for and against + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:
You will hear 5 people talking about their dogs.
For each recording (1–5), decide why each person got their dog.
Do not use any letter more than once. There are three letters you do not need.

A — To teach their children responsibility.
B — For companionship.
C — For protection.
D — For the exercise.
E — To breed them.
F — To give them a home.
G — For fun and play.
H — To improve their children's health.
rights: A — To teach their children responsibility.
F — To give them a home.
H — To improve their children's health.

pairs.r: A — To teach their children responsibility.
F — To give them a home.

qs.exp: Prema ključu: 1=C, 2=D, 3=A, 4=F, 5=E.

qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q6 = C (His caring nature).

qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q7 = B (To make a point).

You will hear two friends talking about cookery courses.
Decide which course (A–C) each question (14–19) refers to.

A = Albert Cookery School
B = Bakewell Cookery School
C = Clough Cookery School

Which course…
items: 15 — is taught by a famous chef?
16 — requires participants to bring special equipment?

pairs.l: 15 — is taught by a famous chef?
16 — requires participants to bring special equipment?

qs.q:
You hear a radio interview with the musician Grey Jackson.

Grey first learned to play…
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q20 = B (the guitar).

qs.q: Grey's first gig took place…
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q21 = A (at a garage).

qs.q: On stage, Grey feels…
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q22 = C (excited).

qs.q: The music Grey now plays is…

qs.q: Grey next plans to…
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q25 = C (appear at an award ceremony).

qs.q:
Banning proms? — Which person…

A=Ashton (sees both sides, alcohol one issue, advises safety/smart decisions, let teens choose)
B=Ben (principal banned prom, met with parents/teachers, agreed it was right, kids survived)
C=Carlie (media hype exaggerated, teens drink every weekend anyway, fashion reflection of culture, keep proms)
D=Deanne (banning leads to secret dances/black market, proms help alienated/depressed teens)
E=Ethan (media/society set glamour bar too high, unaffordable for some, schools should set limits/make affordable)
F=Faith (prom needs makeover, ritual about popularity/wealth, advocates non-prom party instead)

0. talks about personal experience? [B=Ben: 'the principal at my son's school']
1. finds the prom a regular feature of social life?
2. agrees the prom equals unacceptable behaviour?
3. believes alcohol is not a problem only at proms?
4. thinks proms have little to do with achievement?
5. mentions teenagers' mental health?
6. proposes a new kind of celebration?
7. raises the question of social inequality?
8. thinks the choice should be left to teenagers?
9. thinks banning proms could lead to unlawful activities?
10. sees no problem in the costs of a prom?
11. puts the responsibility on educational institutions?
12. thinks a prom mirrors social trends?
items: 1 — finds the prom a regular feature of social life?
2 — agrees the prom equals unacceptable behaviour?
3 — believes alcohol is not a problem only at proms?
4 — thinks proms have little to do with achievement?
6 — proposes a new kind of celebration?
7 — raises the question of social inequality?
8 — thinks the choice should be left to teenagers?
9 — thinks banning proms could lead to unlawful activities?
10 — sees no problem in the costs of a prom?
11 — puts the responsibility on educational institutions?
12 — thinks a prom mirrors social trends?

pairs.l: 1 — finds the prom a regular feature of social life?
2 — agrees the prom equals unacceptable behaviour?
3 — believes alcohol is not a problem only at proms?
4 — thinks proms have little to do with achievement?
6 — proposes a new kind of celebration?
7 — raises the question of social inequality?
8 — thinks the choice should be left to teenagers?
9 — thinks banning proms could lead to unlawful activities?
10 — sees no problem in the costs of a prom?
11 — puts the responsibility on educational institutions?
12 — thinks a prom mirrors social trends?

qs.exp: 1=F (Faith: 'It has always been part of our culture, a big deal'). 2=B (Ben: 'alcohol and drugs swamp the event... financial decadence and vanity'). 3=C (Carlie: 'teenagers drink every weekend, don't they?'). 4=E (Ethan: 'it's about glamour, not merits'). 5=D (Deanne: 'teenagers seem increasingly alienated, distant and even depressed'). 6=F (Faith: 'I would advocate a big non-prom party instead'). 7=E (Ethan: 'students who just want to celebrate... but cannot afford it'). 8=A (Ashton: 'Give them a chance to choose'). 9=D (Deanne: 'inevitably lead to secret illegal dances and renting tuxedos from unlicensed suppliers'). 10=C (Carlie: 'It's okay if girls want to dress up'). 11=E (Ethan: 'I think schools should set limits and say what is acceptable and make it affordable for all'). 12=C (Carlie: 'proms are a reflection of a generation's current fashions and dance – a reflection of our larger culture').

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory in schools

"These contemporary exploits have fostered a recent craze for this mind-training board game."

The Armenians are very much into chess in modern times because…
A chess has always been a national obsession.
B they wish to beat other former Soviet states.
C it is an obligatory part of the primary school curriculum.
D their chess players have been successful.
opts: chess has always been a national obsession.
they wish to beat other former Soviet states.
it is an obligatory part of the primary school curriculum.
their chess players have been successful.
qs.exp: 'These contemporary EXPLOITS have FOSTERED A RECENT CRAZE' = uspjesi šahista potaknuli suvremenu ludost za šahom = D.

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"The education minister says taking the pastime into the classroom will help nurture a sense of organisation among schoolchildren and will teach them the importance of taking care of their duties."

Why did the Armenians decide to introduce chess in primary school?
A To maintain Armenia's status as one of the strongest chess-playing countries.
B To honour their long chess-playing tradition.
C To develop schoolchildren's awareness of responsibility.
D To make the Armenian school system the best in the world.
opts: To maintain Armenia's status as one of the strongest chess-playing countries.
To honour their long chess-playing tradition.
To develop schoolchildren's awareness of responsibility.
To make the Armenian school system the best in the world.
qs.exp: 'Will teach them the importance of TAKING CARE OF THEIR DUTIES' = razvijanje osjećaja odgovornosti = C.

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"Chess will certainly teach him to think logically and improvise, as those are indispensable qualities in life."

What does David's family expect from their son's chess playing?
A To bring him and his family more money in the future.
B To make him part of the national chess team.
C To enable him to beat the local chess whiz kid.
D To help him make rational choices and be resourceful.
opts: To bring him and his family more money in the future.
To make him part of the national chess team.
To enable him to beat the local chess whiz kid.
To help him make rational choices and be resourceful.
qs.exp: 'Chess will certainly teach him to THINK LOGICALLY AND IMPROVISE' = racionalne odluke i snalažljivost = D.

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"'By playing chess in class, the children think they're playing, while they are actually doing some serious thinking all the time.' 'It is a great way to cross over between having a true hard-core curriculum and giving young children the chance to play and have fun.'"

What does the US chess expert think about Armenia's primary school curriculum?
A It is well balanced.
B It is very difficult.
C It has a good campaign.
D It puts focus on children's fun.
opts: It puts focus on children's fun.
qs.exp: 'A great way to CROSS OVER BETWEEN having a hard-core curriculum AND giving children the chance to play' = dobra ravnoteža = A (well balanced).

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"There are some objections to outbursts of bad temper when they lose, and sometimes tears."

A drawback of children playing chess at an early age is that it can…
A teach children to hide their emotions.
B lead to children developing an obsessive addiction.
C lead to children behaving poorly when defeated.
D result in children playing like adults.
opts: teach children to hide their emotions.
lead to children developing an obsessive addiction.
lead to children behaving poorly when defeated.
result in children playing like adults.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA film: vizualni efekti, zvuk, brže, dostupno širem publici. PROTIV: knjiga daje više detalja, vlastita mašta, dublja karakterizacija, originalni autor. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (for and against + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:
Pocket Money — Which person…

A=Anna Marie (youngest of 3 sisters, sisters stole her money, hid it from them)
B=Burt (locked it in special box, too precious to spend, now regrets not spending it on fun)
C=Collin (only mate with pocket money, paid for outings, close friendships formed)
D=Dianne (waited eagerly for Fridays, ran to shop, bought sweets/chocolates, happiest memories)
E=Ellen (parents gave less than her mates, had to be selective about music, learned value of money)
F=Frederick (only kid with pocket money in poor neighbourhood, hid what he bought, didn't want to stand out)

0. felt they did not have enough pocket money? [E=Ellen]
1. saved their pocket money?
2. shared their pocket money?
3. spent their pocket money quickly?
4. spent their pocket money on going out?
5. bought food with their pocket money?
6. bought records with their pocket money?
7. did not receive regular pocket money?
8. looked forward to getting their pocket money?
9. now regrets what they did with their pocket money?
10. says having pocket money helped them later?
11. felt embarrassed about their pocket money?
12. hid their pocket money?
items: 4 — spent their pocket money on going out?
5 — bought food with their pocket money?
6 — bought records with their pocket money?
7 — did not receive regular pocket money?
8 — looked forward to getting their pocket money?
9 — now regrets what they did with their pocket money?
10 — says having pocket money helped them later?
11 — felt embarrassed about their pocket money?

pairs.l: 4 — spent their pocket money on going out?
5 — bought food with their pocket money?
6 — bought records with their pocket money?
7 — did not receive regular pocket money?
8 — looked forward to getting their pocket money?
9 — now regrets what they did with their pocket money?
10 — says having pocket money helped them later?
11 — felt embarrassed about their pocket money?

qs.exp: 1=B (Burt: 'put it in a special box which I could lock'). 2=C (Collin: 'I was the one who paid for it'). 3=D (Dianne: 'I would run out... straight to the shop'). 4=C (Collin: 'wanted to see a film or something, I was the one who paid'). 5=D (Dianne: 'sweets, chocolates and crisps'). 6=E (Ellen: 'getting the new releases of various bands'). 7=A (Anna Marie: 'I didn't get it very often'). 8=D (Dianne: 'I could hardly wait for my dad to come home on Friday'). 9=B (Burt: 'now I know there is no point in dying rich, and I WISH I HAD SPENT my pocket money on records and games'). 10=E (Ellen: 'that wasn't such a bad thing, because I LEARNED THE VALUE OF MONEY and even today I'm careful how I spend it'). 11=F (Frederick: 'I didn't want to appear different from the others, or have the role of the rich kid'). 12=A (Anna Marie: 'I used to immediately put it somewhere where my sisters couldn't find it').

B How curious the whale was.

C He was actually able to touch the whale.
D It helped him to choose his profession.
opts: He had never realised how curious whales were.
It was the first time he had seen a whale.
He was actually able to touch the whale.
It helped him to choose his profession.

C ordinary people.
D dead whales.

Working with Whales

What the author enjoys most about his work is the chance to…

Because there are so many different kinds.
Because of the fact they are so enormous.

D This is quite an impressive number.
E But this will take some time to do.
F They seem very, very small.

H It's a long, long way.
opts: A — A lot of nothingness until the next bit of something.
B — We have found planets that are big and hot.
C — However, it's rather slow on a cosmic scale.
D — This is quite an impressive number.
E — But this will take some time to do.
F — They seem very, very small.
G — They can't see you and me.
H — It's a long, long way.

qs.q:
The White House

"The site was (25) ___ in 1790 by America's first president, George Washington."

A favoured
B decided
C elected
D chosen
qs.exp: 'The site was CHOSEN in 1790 by George Washington' — 'chosen' (izabrano/odabrano mjesto). 'Elected' = izabran za položaj, ne za lokaciju.

qs.q:
The White House

"He put in considerable effort in the construction. (26) ___, he was the only President not to live in it."

A Nevertheless
B Although
C In fact
D So
qs.exp: 'Considerable effort in construction. NEVERTHELESS, he was the only President not to live in it.' — 'nevertheless' za kontrast (trud, ali ipak nije u njemu živio).

qs.q:
The White House

"In 1800, the construction was (27) ___ completed and President John Adams moved in."

A approximately
B broadly
C closely
D nearly
qs.exp: 'Construction was NEARLY completed' — 'nearly' = skoro, gotovo (adverb uz pridjeve/participe).

qs.q:
The White House

"After being torched by British troops, it was rebuilt according to the (28) ___ plans."

A authentic
B genuine
C primary
D original
qs.exp: 'Rebuilt according to the ORIGINAL plans' — fiksna kolokacija: original plans = prvotni, izvorni planovi.

qs.q:
The White House

"The most important (29) ___ was the construction of the East Wing and the West Wing."

A enhancement
B enrichment
C expansion
D exterior
qs.exp: 'Most important EXPANSION was the construction of the East Wing' — 'expansion' = proširenje (fizičko proširenje zgrade).

qs.q:
The White House

"The West Wing, which (30) ___ the famous 'Oval Office'."

A encloses
B contains
C keeps
D holds
qs.exp: 'The West Wing, which CONTAINS the famous Oval Office' — 'contain' = sadržavati, imati u sebi (za zgrade/prostore).

qs.q:
The White House

"The building wasn't called the White House (31) ___ the beginning."

A by
B for
C on
D at
qs.exp: 'Wasn't called the White House AT the beginning' — fiksni izraz: at the beginning = na početku.

qs.q:
The White House

"President Theodore Roosevelt gave it (32) ___ present name in 1901."

A that
B this
C the
D its
qs.exp: 'Gave it ITS present name' — posvojna zamjenica 'its' (gave the building its name = dati zgradi njezino ime).

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"English literature provides the richest source of silly place names (33) ___ the world."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'The richest source IN the world' — prijedlog 'in' uz superlativne konstrukcije (the richest in the world).

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"A complete list of extraordinarily silly places is by no (34) ___ all fiction and fantasy."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'By no MEANS all fiction' — fiksni izraz: by no means = nikako, nipošto.

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"What (35) ___ London's Ha-Ha Road, or for example Dogpoo Lane?"

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'What ABOUT London's Ha-Ha Road?' — fiksni izraz: what about = a što kažeš za, a kako je s.

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"So who are the people (36) ___ enviable job it is to christen these places?"

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'The people WHOSE enviable job it is' — posvojni relativni prilog 'whose' (people + their job = whose job).

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"Road names like Baker Street (37) ___ traditionally been used to tell us something about the inhabitants."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Road names HAVE traditionally been used' — present perfect uz 'traditionally' (dugogodišnja tradicija).

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"So what (38) ___ we to think of people who spend their lives on Catbrain Hill?"

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'What ARE we to think of...' — konstrukcija: be to + infinitive = što nam je reći/misliti (u retorskom pitanju).

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"Instead of (39) ___ our streets sound cosy and pleasant, maybe we should call them Dracula Drive."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Instead of MAKING our streets sound cosy' — 'instead of' + gerund; make + object + adjective = učiniti nešto zvučati...

qs.q:
Silly Place Names

"That could at least keep strangers (40) ___ from our homes."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Keep strangers AWAY from our homes' — frazalni glagol: keep away (from) = držati podalje od.

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that the more we use our smartphones the less we use our brains."

Discuss arguments for and against this view and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA (smartfoni = manje razmišljamo): ovisnost, autocorrect smanjuje pismenost, GPS zamjenjuje orijentaciju, Google zamjenjuje pamćenje. PROTIV: vježbamo um aplikacijama, dostupnost znanja, kreativnost, komunikacija. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (for and against + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:
You will hear 5 people talking about their eating habits.
For each recording (1–5), match the statement (A–H) with the speaker.
Do not use any letter more than once. There are three letters you do not need.

This speaker…
A — likes traditional food.
B — likes exotic food.
C — is a vegetarian.
D — is a nutritionist.
E — eats fast food.
F — likes to cook.
G — is anorexic.
H — is on a diet.
qs.exp: Prema ključu: 1=F, 2=H, 3=A, 4=E, 5=B.

qs.q:
Extreme Sports — Which person…

A=Adam (rock climbing — ignored as child, solo climbing)
B=Benjamin (bungee jumping — waited until 18, once and never again)
C=Connor (BMX — grandpa helped, won cup)

E=Ethan (surfing — injured, watching TV until recovery)
F=Finley (mountain bike spectator — brother does downhill racing)

0. likes fighting gravity? [E=Ethan: 'catching and riding waves']
1. was quick to make progress?
2. couldn't cope with the adrenaline rush?
3. was afraid at the beginning?
4. was too frightened to try the sport?
5. did not have his parents' permission?
6. felt ignored by his friends?
7. could not afford the equipment?
8. enjoys watching the sport?
9. won a competition?
10. enjoys the danger?
11. wishes he had done the sport?
12. has to take a break from the sport?
items: 2 — couldn't cope with the adrenaline rush?
4 — was too frightened to try the sport?
5 — did not have his parents' permission?
11 — wishes he had done the sport?
12 — has to take a break from the sport?

pairs.l: 2 — couldn't cope with the adrenaline rush?
4 — was too frightened to try the sport?
5 — did not have his parents' permission?
11 — wishes he had done the sport?
12 — has to take a break from the sport?

qs.exp: 1=E (Ethan: 'very soon I was riding Nu-skool'). 2=B (Benjamin: 'just too much excitement for me. Once and never again.'). 3=A (Adam: 'I felt uneasy at first'). 4=F (Finley: 'quite enough for me to ride an ordinary bike'). 5=F (Finley: 'My parents would never have allowed it'). 6=D (Daniel: 'they never asked me to join in'). 7=C (Connor: 'parents generally disapproved of spending money on extreme sports'). 8=F (Finley: 'I always go to watch him'). 9=C (Connor: 'won the club cup last year'). 10=B (Benjamin: 'attracted me was the thought of the danger'). 11=D (Daniel: 'I'm sure I would have been able to do it'). 12=E (Ethan: 'having to watch it on TV until I recover').

qs.q:
Going Underground

"Although I passed my driving test, living and working in a crowded city of ten million people, I could never see the point in owning a car. I suppose it's just that I've got used to it after all this time."

Why does the author use the underground railway?
A It's cheaper than other means of transport.
B It allows her to escape the bad weather.
C It's something she does out of habit.
D She has never learnt how to drive.
opts: It's cheaper than other means of transport.
It allows her to escape the bad weather.
It's something she does out of habit.
She has never learnt how to drive.
qs.exp: 'I suppose it's just that I've GOT USED TO IT after all this time' = navika = C (out of habit).

qs.q:
Going Underground

"I notice that, unlike me, many passengers use their daily trips as an opportunity to catch up with their unfinished business. There are always commuters with their laptops or going over reports. Some simply like to watch the capital's inhabitants... I'm definitely one of the former."

The author likes to spend her time on the underground…
A getting some work done.
B observing other people.
C reading a good book.
D having a short nap.
qs.exp: 'Some simply like to WATCH the capital's inhabitants... I'm definitely one of the FORMER' → 'former' refers to watching people = B (observing other people).

qs.q:
Going Underground

"I'm convinced that the majority of commuters would consider the consumption of snacks such as burgers to be the most anti-social practice on our journeys. Loud music on iPods or phones, especially rap and heavy metal, probably wouldn't be far behind."

Which behaviour does the author dislike most on the underground?
A Reading newspapers.
B Playing music.
C Kissing.
D Eating.
qs.exp: 'Consumption of snacks such as burgers to be the MOST ANTI-SOCIAL practice' = jelo = D (Eating).

qs.q:
Going Underground

"A proud-looking old man getting upset when a young woman got up and vacated her seat for him. 'Young lady. Do you think I'm too weak to stand on my own two feet?' he roared. She was only trying to help. The poor girl was horrified."

Why did the author tell the little story in the fifth paragraph?
A To show that you should be careful not to offend people.
B To show that funny things happen on the underground.
C To show that people can be rude on public transport.
D To show that old people can be very independent.
opts: To show that you should be careful not to offend people.
To show that funny things happen on the underground.
To show that people can be rude on public transport.
To show that old people can be very independent.
qs.exp: Priča pokazuje da je djevojka htjela pomoći ali je uvrijedila starca — pazi da ne uvrijediš ljude = A (be careful not to offend people).

qs.q:
Going Underground

"They are a distinguishing characteristic of our transport system. It'd be a shame if busking was made illegal."

What's the author's opinion of the musicians who play in underground stations?
A They are a special feature of the underground system.
B They create a negative impression of the city.
C There should be a law passed against them.
D They are not as good as they used to be.
opts: They are a special feature of the underground system.
They create a negative impression of the city.
There should be a law passed against them.
They are not as good as they used to be.
qs.exp: 'A DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTIC of our transport system' = posebnost = A (a special feature).

qs.q:
Going Underground — What was the author's aim in writing the article?
A To propose improvements to the underground.
B To offer a personal view of the underground.
C To give advice on using the underground.
D To criticise the underground system.
opts: To propose improvements to the underground.
To offer a personal view of the underground.
To give advice on using the underground.
qs.exp: Cijeli tekst je osobni doživljaj autorice na podzemnoj željeznici — to je osobni prikaz = B (personal view).

F If we're in serious trouble, then we can obviously get help.

"Pollen is the name given to the fine powder produced by plants or flowers to fertilise (25) ___ plants or flowers."

Hay Fever

"It (26) ___ up to one in five people in the United Kingdom at some point in their life."

A influences
B impacts
C affects
D effects

qs.q:
Hay Fever

"It's the fifth most common chronic disease and often first develops (27) ___ the teenage years."

A during
B when
C while
D over
qs.exp: 'First develops DURING the teenage years' — 'during' uz imeničku frazu (the teenage years). 'When/while' idu uz surečenice.

qs.q:
Hay Fever

"You are more likely to develop hay fever if you (28) ___ have asthma."

A already
B before
C ever
D yet
qs.exp: 'If you ALREADY have asthma' = ako već imate astmu. 'Already' uz present simple za postojeće stanje.

qs.q:
Hay Fever

"Sometimes they are so bad that they (29) ___ with school or work."

A interfere
B meddle
C intrude
D mingle
qs.exp: 'INTERFERE with school or work' — fiksna kolokacija: interfere with = ometati, smetati (u negativnom smislu za aktivnosti).

qs.q:
Hay Fever

"Runny nose, watery eyes and (30) ___ of concentration are particularly unpleasant."

A shortage
B absence
C losing
D loss
qs.exp: 'LOSS of concentration' — fiksna kolokacija: loss of concentration (gubitak koncentracije). 'Shortage' = nedostatak resursa.

qs.q:
Hay Fever

"The symptoms tend to be less severe if you stay inside as (31) ___ as possible."

A many
B much
C more
D most
qs.exp: 'Stay inside as MUCH as possible' — fiksni izraz: as much as possible = što je više moguće. 'Much' uz nebrojivu/apstraktnu imenicu (količinu vremena).

qs.q:
Hay Fever

"(32) ___, avoid places like parks or fields especially early in the morning or evening."

A Therefore
B Moreover

qs.exp: 'After a few crashes, he was on his way' = naučio sam, prateći brata ali praktički SAM = D (on his own). Brat mu je bio uzor ali nije ga aktivno učio.

it was the most practical way to get around.
he was thrilled at the speed he could go.

qs.exp: 'He had the PERFECT BUILD for a long-distance cyclist' — trener ga je odmah primijetio zbog tijela = A (His body/physique).

qs.q:
Rainy Days

"Britain is an island country and the surrounding sea gives England a (25) ___ climate."

A variety
B various
C varied
D variant
qs.exp: 'A VARIED climate' — pridjev 'varied' = raznovrstan (ispred imenice). 'Various' = razni (ne ispred 'climate' s članom 'a').

qs.q:
Rainy Days

"But (26) ___ its ever-changing weather, the climate in Britain is mostly mild and temperate."

A despite
B in spite
C regardless
D with regard to
qs.exp: 'DESPITE its ever-changing weather' — 'despite' + imenička skupina. 'In spite of' tražilo bi 'of'. 'Regardless of' tražilo bi 'of'.

qs.q:
Rainy Days

"(27) ___ influence on the climate is the warming of the waters around the land by the Gulf Stream."

A Main
B A main
C One main
D The main
qs.exp: 'THE MAIN influence on the climate' — određeni član 'the' za superlativni/jedinstven pojam (the main = glavni, jedini).

qs.q:
Rainy Days

"It helps (28) ___ winters less cold compared with other landlocked nations."

A in keeping
B keeping
C keep
D to have kept
qs.exp: 'It helps KEEP winters less cold' — 'help' + infinitiv bez 'to' (bare infinitive): help keep. 'Help' se ne slaže s gerundom.

qs.q:
Rainy Days

"British summers are cooler than (29) ___ on the continent."

A these
B those
C this
D that
qs.exp: 'Cooler than THOSE on the continent' — 'those' = onima (British summers = plural → those summers on the continent).

qs.q:
Rainy Days

"The temperature is subject to (30) ___ extremes – it is rarely above 32°C or below -10°C."

A few
B little
C some
D less
qs.exp: 'Subject to FEW extremes' — 'few' uz brojivu imenicu množine (extremes). 'Little' uz nebrojivu. 'Few' = malo, rijetko.

qs.q:
Rainy Days

"(31) ___ average, March to June are the driest months."

A in
B by
C at
D on
qs.exp: 'ON average' — fiksna kolokacija: on average = prosječno, u prosjeku.

qs.q:
Rainy Days

A will visit
B visit
C have visited
D will have visited
qs.exp: 'If you VISIT the mountainous areas' — uvjetna rečenica 1. tipa (realni uvjet): if + present simple.

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Not only among linguists... BUT also among all interested' — fiksni izraz: not only... but (also) = ne samo... nego i.

qs.q:
Language Death

"A leading commentator dealing (34) ___ language issues, David Crystal, asks the fundamental question."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Dealing WITH language issues' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: deal with = baviti se (nečim).

qs.q:
Language Death

"Investigates what is (35) ___ done to reduce its impact."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'What is BEING done' — present continuous passive: is being done = što se trenutno radi.

qs.q:
Language Death

"Only 600 of the 6,000 or (36) ___ languages in the world are 'safe' from the threat of extinction."

(Upiši jednu riječ)

qs.q:
Language Death

"The world will, by the end of the twenty-first century, (37) ___ dominated by a small number of major languages."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Will BE dominated by' — future simple passive: will + be + past participle.

qs.q:
Language Death

"Language Death provides a stimulating account of this alarming trend, (38) ___, like the large-scale destruction of the environment, is both peculiarly modern and increasingly global."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'An alarming trend, WHICH... is both peculiarly modern' — ne-restriktivna relativna zamjenica 'which' (uz zarez, odnosi se na 'trend').

qs.q:
Language Death

"Language Death includes practical advice for anyone interested in pursuing the subject (39) ___."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Pursuing the subject FURTHER' — 'further' = dalje, dublje (pursue further = istražiti dublje).

qs.q:
Language Death

"David Crystal is a leading authority (40) ___ language."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'A leading authority ON language' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: an authority on = autoritet za/o nečemu.

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that social media like Facebook are replacing proper social life. Others say they enrich social communication."

Discuss both points of view and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA zamjenu: smanjuje fizičke kontakte, površni online odnosi, ovisnost, manje kvalitetnog vremena s obitelji. PROTIV (tj. ZA obogaćivanje): ostajanje u kontaktu s dalekima, dijeljenje iskustava, brza komunikacija. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:

D — Imitation.

qs.exp: Prema službenom ključu: 1=G, 2=D, 3=B, 4=F, 5=C.

qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q9 = A (Their exam results).

qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q10 = C (To study).

in search of fame and fortune.

qs.q:
Trips to London — During their trip to London, which person…

A=Alisha (university interview, nervous, slept badly, thought she failed, accepted a week later)
B=Bailey (needed direction in life, wandered, met old woman in Green Park, felt better)
C=Chris (awful weekend, taxi accident, noisy hotel, no good shopping, poured with rain)
D=Daniela (got lost in changed area, unexpectedly met old school friend)
E=Evelyn (scared of flying, turbulence, didn't want to go, parents' friends turned out wonderful)
F=Frederick (dream to see Wembley match, alone among fans in hotel, happiest memories next day)

0. watched a football match? [F=Frederick]
1. was happily surprised?
2. experienced flight anxiety?
3. realised a wish?
4. was involved in an accident?
5. met an old friend?
6. felt they had failed?
7. stayed in a noisy hotel?
8. got lost?
9. slept badly?
10. felt lonely?
11. wished they had not gone?
12. gained in confidence?
qs.exp: 1=E (Evelyn: 'they turned out to be really nice, not what I had expected... fantastic time'). 2=E (Evelyn: 'dead scared of flying... turbulence on the way there didn't help'). 3=F (Frederick: 'It had always been my dream to watch a match at Wembley'). 4=C (Chris: 'someone knocked into my taxi'). 5=D (Daniela: 'someone I hadn't seen since secondary school'). 6=A (Alisha: 'I left the interview feeling good for nothing, sure that I hadn't been good enough'). 7=C (Chris: 'traffic noise was far too loud, so I had to find a different one'). 8=D (Daniela: 'I had no idea where I was'). 9=A (Alisha: 'I kept waking up during the night'). 10=F (Frederick: 'feeling sad I had no one to share this experience with'). 11=A (Alisha: 'I thought it would have been better if I had stayed at home'). 12=B (Bailey: 'felt better about myself and ready to resume my life').

qs.q:
The Face of the Games

"I do know that it has justified the many years of hard training I'd put in for that moment."

How does she feel about winning Olympic gold?
A Elated.
B Exhausted.
C Confused.
D Justified.

The Face of the Games

"I had proved to myself that I was the best in the world. It made all the years of self-sacrifice worthwhile."

D — Nevertheless, students appreciate things the computer can help them do.

F — There's no other way they could have got such up-to-date information.
G — The only difference is that these boys are being given design tips by a computer.
H — Each department undertakes to teach students particular skills.

qs.q:

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA odgovornost prestaje s 18: punoljetnost, pravna neovisnost, pravo na vlastite odluke. ZA odgovornost ne prestaje nikad: roditeljska ljubav, financijska podrška, životno iskustvo. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:
Schooltime — Which person…

A=Alexander (hated school, bullied, poor family same clothes, French teacher called him stupid, physics teacher favourite)
B=Bethany (strict teachers, cheated in tests, extra home lessons, wishes she could go back)
C=Callum (lived for breaks/playtime, cooked meals at school, parents felt he could do better)
D=Daisy (not expected to stay on, couldn't stand school food, PE best, English teacher favourite)
E=Edward (school kept him off streets, no neighbourhood friends, school play, football Saturdays, left at 16)
F=Freya (rebel clique, cheated massively, dress code restrictions, didn't want school to end)

0. had parents who were not rich? [A=Alexander: 'because my parents were poor']
1. was good at sport?
2. felt he/she disappointed his/her parents?
3. disliked school meals?
4. disliked a subject because of the teacher?
5. was sorry to leave school?
6. felt under pressure to cheat?
7. enjoyed playtime most?
8. went to a school with a strict dress code?
9. wanted to leave school as soon as he/she could?
10. did not have friends at school?
11. would like to go to school again?
12. was a teacher's favourite?
items: 4 — disliked a subject because of the teacher?
8 — went to a school with a strict dress code?
9 — wanted to leave school as soon as he/she could?
10 — did not have friends at school?
11 — would like to go to school again?

pairs.l: 4 — disliked a subject because of the teacher?
8 — went to a school with a strict dress code?
9 — wanted to leave school as soon as he/she could?
10 — did not have friends at school?
11 — would like to go to school again?

qs.exp: 1=E (Edward: 'travelling on Saturdays to play football for the school'). 2=C (Callum: 'my parents never said it, I'm sure they felt I could have done better'). 3=D (Daisy: 'couldn't stand the food and took sandwiches to school'). 4=A (Alexander: 'My French teacher called me stupid, so I couldn't even listen to the language after that'). 5=F (Freya: 'Crazy as it was, I didn't want it to end'). 6=B (Bethany: 'I knew that my parents would be very disappointed...so I often cheated in tests'). 7=C (Callum: 'I lived for the breaks... best was the lunch break'). 8=F (Freya: 'all sorts of restrictions on how we could behave and what we should wear'). 9=D (Daisy: 'wasn't expected to stay on at school after the minimum school-leaving age'). 10=E (Edward: 'none of my classmates lived near me, and I had no one to play with'). 11=B (Bethany: 'I wish I could have that time again'). 12=D (Daisy: 'My English teacher for some reason treated me better than the others').

0. used to be in the armed forces? [A=Alan: 'former member of the military']

2. had poor results?

7. taught a sport where it wasn't popular?
8. used out-of-date tactics?

10. was good at demonstrating what to do?

items: 5 — thought subject grades were equally important?
7 — taught a sport where it wasn't popular?
9 — had an influence on their career?
10 — was good at demonstrating what to do?
11 — was forced to change their approach by the players?
12 — brought about a dramatic improvement in results?

However, she was truly amazing'). 5=E (Ed: 'expected us to get good marks in school studies too'). 6=A (Alan: 'push us to the limit... punishing schedule'). 7=E (Ed: 'basketball was definitely a minority sport'). 8=C (Chris: 'playing systems that nobody else had used for decades'). 9=B (Bella: 'Her example inspired me to study to become a PE teacher'). 10=D (Dora: 'absolutely brilliant at showing us how to play all the various shots'). 11=F (Florence: 'players threatened to report her to principal. She calmed down after that'). 12=A (Alan: 'We went from completely rubbish to one of the top teams in the area').

g — reduced need for leader to tell what to do

The water RUINED OUR WALLS'). 8=D (Doris: 'if only they had SPOKEN TO US ABOUT IT BEFOREHAND'). 9=C (Conrad: 'made an awful MESS in the yard'). 10=B (Brian: 'they're always RESPECTFUL'). 11=D (Doris: 'We had to go to COURT to settle everything'). 12=E (Ella: 'they also HELP US FIX THINGS IN THE HOUSE').

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"We just thought that it would be A LAUGH TO TRY OURSELVES."

The author and his friends decided to start a band because…
A they liked the energy of the music they heard.
B they thought that they would have good fun.
C they wanted people to hear their political views.
D they were impressed by the image of punk.
opts: they liked the energy of the music they heard.
they thought that they would have good fun.
they wanted people to hear their political views.
they were impressed by the image of punk.
qs.exp: 'We just thought it would be A LAUGH TO TRY OURSELVES' = htjeli su se zabaviti = B.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"We wanted to send a message... that it DIDN'T MATTER WHO YOU WERE, because you could START A BAND TOO."

What does the author say about the band's music?
A It improved a lot as time passed.
B It showed anyone could be in a group.
C It was influenced by various styles.
D It was not as important as the words.
opts: It improved a lot as time passed.
It showed anyone could be in a group.
It was influenced by various styles.
It was not as important as the words.
qs.exp: 'Didn't matter WHO YOU WERE, because you could START A BAND TOO' = glazba pokazuje da to može svako = B.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"The company WOULDN'T RELEASE IT. They said the politics were too risky. We weren't going to stand for CENSORSHIP, so we SET UP OUR OWN COMPANY."

Why did the band start their own record company?
A They wanted to help new groups record albums.
B They wanted to make records that were affordable.
C They wanted to sell more and reach more people.
D They wanted to sing about whatever they wished.
opts: They wanted to help new groups record albums.
They wanted to make records that were affordable.
They wanted to sell more and reach more people.
They wanted to sing about whatever they wished.
qs.exp: 'We weren't going to stand for CENSORSHIP' = odbijali su da im govore što smiju pjevati = D.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"We knew they would TWIST AND DISTORT EVERYTHING WE SAID."

The band didn't do interviews with the media because…
A they believed journalists were not interested in the truth.
B they felt TV and newspapers were only interested in money.
C they wanted to avoid too much publicity about their lives.
D they wanted to promote smaller publications.
opts: they believed journalists were not interested in the truth.
they felt TV and newspapers were only interested in money.
they wanted to avoid too much publicity about their lives.
they wanted to promote smaller publications.
qs.exp: 'We knew they would TWIST AND DISTORT EVERYTHING WE SAID' = novinari ne bi govorili istinu = A.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"You can't RAISE KIDS when you're constantly touring."

Why did the group stop playing?
A To bring up their families.
B To give new bands a chance.
C To start a book company.
D To take a break from touring.
opts: To give new bands a chance.
To take a break from touring.
qs.exp: 'You can't RAISE KIDS when you're constantly touring' = morali brinuti o obiteljima = A.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"Before then, hardly anyone was a vegetarian and no one protested against injustice. Nowadays, there are MANY MORE PEOPLE LIKE THAT. We PLAYED A ROLE IN THAT."

What does the author think the band achieved?
A They contributed to improving animal rights.
B They had an effect on the music industry.
C They helped bring about changes in attitudes.
D They were a role model to young people.
opts: They contributed to improving animal rights.
They had an effect on the music industry.
They helped bring about changes in attitudes.
They were a role model to young people.
qs.exp: 'Before, nobody was vegetarian and no one protested. Nowadays many more people like that. We PLAYED A ROLE IN THAT' = pomogli promijeniti stavove = C.

A is
B was

A as

A away

(Upiši jednu riječ)

(Upiši jednu riječ)

The History of Baseball

"The first recorded baseball game (35) ___ place a year later."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'The first game TOOK place a year later' — fiksna kolokacija: take place = odvijati se, dogoditi se.

qs.q:
The History of Baseball

"Cartwright's Knickerbocker Base Ball Club lost (36) ___ New York Base Ball Club."

(Upiši jednu riječ)

The History of Baseball

(Upiši jednu riječ)

The History of Baseball

The History of Baseball

"The league grew and so (39) ___ the expenses of playing."

(Upiši jednu riječ)

The History of Baseball

"there was (40) ___ way they could compete with the professional teams."

(Upiši jednu riječ)

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that there should be limits to what students can wear at school. Others say there should not."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA ograničenja: jednakost, disciplina, smanjenje socijalnih razlika, fokus na učenje. PROTIV: sloboda izražavanja, kreativnost, individualni identitet. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (školska odjeća). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi. Napomena: travanjski rok — nema ispita slušanja.

items: 1 — finds it crowded where they shop?
2 — can find going to stores stressful?
4 — likes to combine shopping with another activity?

6 — often buys things that they don't need?
9 — sometimes buys nothing when they go shopping?

2 — can find going to stores stressful?
4 — likes to combine shopping with another activity?

What did Adam enjoy most about working in his uncle's restaurant?

Adam Walker

Adam Walker

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"What initially came to mind was that maybe it occupies too many hours of the school timetable. I know that some parents complain that it distracts children from their studies."

At first, the writer thought that some schools had banned competitive sport because…
A it has a negative psychological impact.
B there are a lot of injuries.
C pupils already do enough exercise.
D it takes up too much time.
opts: it has a negative psychological impact.
there are a lot of injuries.
it takes up too much time.
qs.exp: 'What initially came to mind was that maybe it OCCUPIES TOO MANY HOURS of the school timetable' = zauzima previše vremena = D.

"I recall that we came last but one out of twelve teams in our league."

B Second.
C Eleventh.
D Last.
qs.exp: 'Last but ONE out of twelve' = predzadnje od 12 = 11. mjesto = C (Eleventh).

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"Did the experience damage us mentally? I'm still in contact with quite a few of the people who I played with and they appear to have grown up without any lasting effects."

A pointless certain organised sports can be.
B team sports can help keep young people fit.
C losing doesn't necessarily matter to children.
D team sports can help bring people together.
opts: pointless certain organised sports can be.
team sports can help keep young people fit.
losing doesn't necessarily matter to children.
team sports can help bring people together.
qs.exp: 'Did the experience DAMAGE us mentally?... they appear to have grown up WITHOUT any LASTING EFFECTS' = gubitak ne mora štetiti djeci = C.

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"Competition is part of life, so surely it's better to prepare pupils for this rather than protect them from such realities. Learning how to manage both success and failure is a vital lesson."

According to paragraph three, competitive sport can help pupils…
A work successfully in teams.
B cope with life's disappointments.
C perform better at school.
D get a good job after their education.
opts: get a good job after their education.
qs.exp: 'Learning how to MANAGE BOTH SUCCESS AND FAILURE is a vital lesson' = nositi se sa životnim razočaranjima = B.

qs.q:
Is Competitive Sport a Good Thing?

"The result was much better than either I or my trainer had ever expected and was one that was never to be repeated. In fact, it's a result that I still look back on with a certain amount of pride."

The main point in paragraph four is that…
A bad results can help motivate people.
B losing is not necessarily the same as failure.
C sport is a source of pride for people.
D many people no longer play sport as adults.
opts: bad results can help motivate people.
losing is not necessarily the same as failure.
sport is a source of pride for people.
many people no longer play sport as adults.
qs.exp: 'Everything is relative... 19th out of 80... much BETTER THAN EXPECTED... I look back with PRIDE' = gubitak ne znači nužno neuspjeh = B.

qs.q:

qs.exp: 'Activities like aerobics or Pilates are NOT bad... any kind of exercise IS A GOOD THING' = mogu imati pozitivnih učinaka = A.

qs.exp: 1=D (David: food critic, 'dining in exclusive restaurants'). 2=E (Emily: 'kind of therapy for escaping stress'). 3=B (Beatrice: 'graduated as a nutritionist'). 4=A (Anne: 'like a fish out of water... can manage omelettes'). 5=F (Frank: 'diagnosed as a migraine sufferer, dairy products the first thing to go'). 6=A (Anne: 'takeaway would undoubtedly cost the earth'). 7=D (David: 'sample wonderful creations virtually every day... exclusive seafood restaurants'). 8=C (Clive: 'I'm hardly the adventurous type'). 9=B (Beatrice: 'crucial to avoid eating too much red meat'). 10=E (Emily: 'I prefer staying in' — wait, that's Anne. Emily: used to eat in canteen, now cooks at home). 11=C (Clive: 'Organic food... all pass me by'). 12=A (Anne: 'who needs culinary expertise when there's the old microwave?').

qs.q:
Earthrise

"'Earthrise' has become one of history's most influential images. It transformed our view of ourselves. It brought home the awareness that the world was a place we all share together."

According to the author, 'Earthrise' is important because…
A it is the first picture of the Earth.
B it is the most famous picture of the Earth.
C it changed the way people look at the Earth.
D it shows how fragile the Earth is.
opts: it is the first picture of the Earth.
it is the most famous picture of the Earth.
it changed the way people look at the Earth.
it shows how fragile the Earth is.
qs.exp: 'It TRANSFORMED our view of ourselves' = promijenilo način na koji gledamo na Zemlju = C.

qs.q:
Earthrise

"When you see our Earth surrounded by the infinity of space, it makes you feel very small and unimportant."

For the author, 'Earthrise' makes the Earth look…

B helpless.
C insignificant.
D small.
qs.exp: 'Earthrise is a striking reminder of EARTH'S VULNERABILITY. There is nothing that will come to SAVE it.' = nemoćna = B (helpless).

Earthrise

The initial aim of the mission was…

to prepare for a moon landing.

Earthrise

On the first night in space, Borman…

qs.q:

When the Earth rose above the Moon, Anders was…

prepared for landing the first man on the Moon.
raised interest in the space programme.

Dr Martens Shoes

Dr Martens Shoes

qs.exp: 'It MAKES no difference' — fiksna kolokacija: make no difference = nema razlike, nije važno.

qs.q:

Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some say it would be better if there was only one language in the world. Others disagree."

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, složene strukture, bogat vokabular, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q: The author was fascinated by Vesuvius because of…
qs.exp: Autor piše da je osjećao kao da je “ušao u drugi svijet, tako različit od svog” → čudnost (strangeness). Bio je fasciniran različitošću, ne opasnosću ni snagom.

qs.q:
