G — This is particularly true if they’ve been there for a while.
H — In fact, you wouldn’t believe how cruel some people can be to their pets.
qs.exp: Gap (23) je između “sometimes not the owner’s fault” i “particularly upsetting when deliberately mistreated”. B (“some people become too ill to care for their animals”) daje konkretan primjer kad nije vlasnikova krivnja.

qs.q:
Working with animals — gap (24)

“His owners, a young married couple, bought him as a puppy. (24) ___. As a result, he ended up alone in the flat all day while they were at work.”
opts: A — The work can be extremely demanding physically and I was exhausted.
B — For instance, some people become too ill to care for their animals.
C — It can be hard work rising before the sun, especially on cold winter days.
D — Of course, they hadn’t thought about his needs at all.
E — Sometimes we get more unusual guests.
F — That can be quite tough sometimes as they can be quite lively.
G — This is particularly true if they’ve been there for a while.
H — In fact, you wouldn’t believe how cruel some people can be to their pets.
qs.exp: Gap (24) je između “bought him as a puppy” i “As a result, he ended up alone”. D (“Of course, they hadn’t thought about his needs at all”) savršeno objašnjava zašto je završio sam.

qs.q: I had not seen them ___ months.
qs.exp: ‘For months’ (bez ‘some’) ili ‘in months’ (= odavno). Kontekst: “whom I had not seen in months” → ‘in’ u značenju “nijednom u proteklim mjesecima”.

qs.q: I had changed my ___ and moved to a new flat.
qs.exp: ‘Changed my job’ = promijenio posao. Fiksna kolokacija. ‘Work’ je nebroj. i ne ide s ‘changed my’ u ovom kontekstu.

qs.q: I wanted to ___ them all my news.
qs.exp: ‘Tell someone news’ = ispričati nekome vijesti. ‘Tell’ zahtijeva neizravni objekt (them). ‘Say’/‘talk’/‘discuss’ ne odgovaraju strukturi.

qs.q: They were far too interested ___ a film on television.
qs.exp: ‘Interested in’ = zainteresiran za. Fiksna prepozicija.

qs.q: For the next hour I had to ___ the film.
qs.exp: ‘Watch a film’ = gledati film (aktivan, kontinuiran glagol). ‘See a film’ bi bilo ispravno samo za “jesi li vidio taj film?”.

qs.q: I stayed ___ the end of the film.
qs.exp: ‘Stayed until the end’ = ostao do kraja. ‘Until’ za trajanje do nekog trenutka.

qs.q: It has shown me countries with very different ___ from mine.
qs.exp: ‘Customs’ = običaji (kulturalni). ‘Countries with different customs’ je standardna kolokacija.

qs.q: It has enriched my life in many ways. ___, it can become an obsession.
qs.exp: ‘However’ = međutim (suprotnost). Prethodi pohvala TVa, slijedi upozorenje → kontrast.

qs.q: The game contained huge amounts of fake banknotes and plastic hotels and... we all know ___ Monopoly.
qs.exp: ‘Known as’ = poznat kao. Idiom: ‘known as X’.

qs.q: ...it ___ meant to help you sharpen your financial skills.
qs.exp: Pasiv prošlog vremena: ‘it was meant to’ = bilo je zamišljeno da.

qs.q: The game soon became available ___ versions based on many of the world’s most important cities.
qs.exp: ‘Available in versions’ = dostupno u inačicama.

qs.q: It has been one of the most popular games played worldwide ___ since.
qs.exp: ‘Ever since’ = od tada pa nadalje.

qs.q: And, believe it or not, ___ is also a Star Wars Monopoly edition.
qs.exp: Bezlična egzistencijalna konstrukcija: ‘there is’.

qs.q: The game includes locations ___ as Endor Evok Village and Death Star Landing Bay.
qs.exp: ‘Such as’ = poput, kao na primjer. Standardna fraza za nabrajanje primjera.

qs.q: ...you can find all the features keen Monopoly players have come to know and love, like collecting extra money when passing the “Go” sign, or receiving the ever popular card that gets you out of jail ___ free.
qs.exp: ‘Get out of jail for free’ = izlaz iz zatvora besplatno. Ustaljeni izraz iz Monopolyja.

qs.q: ...you can build colonies in space ___ of hotels on Earth.
qs.exp: ‘Instead of’ = umjesto. ‘Colonies instead of hotels’.

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

Some people say that international sports events bring countries closer. Others say they cause bad feelings between countries.
Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.ans: Referentni odgovor — esej mora imati: uvod (teza/anti-teza), tijelo (argumenti za i protiv), zaključak s osobnim mišljenjem. Za: zajednički duh, međukulturni dijalog, sportsko druženje. Protiv: nacionalizam, huliganstvo, medijski pritisak. 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:
You hear 5 people talking about holiday courses they went on.
For each recording (1–5), decide what the speaker had a problem with. Choose from A–H. There are three letters you do not need.
qs.exp: 1=F (bio osamljeniji jer su drugi ostajali u jezičnim grupama), 2=C (izleti su bili bez vodiča, ništa nisu naučili), 3=A (kolegice s hodnika su slavile svake noći), 4=B (tečaj je bio prelak za njegov nivo), 5=E (sve u Švedskoj je preskupo). D, G, H su suvišni.

qs.q: You hear Linda talking to a friend about doing weight training. Why does Linda do it?
qs.exp: Linda kaže: “a group of us girls do it once a week” i “What do I care? We’re just girls who like to have fun.” → drugarstvo (to be with friends).

qs.q: You hear John talking to a friend about next Saturday. What does John decide to do?
qs.exp: John na kraju pristaje otići na planinarenje: “Ok, then.” Roštilj je poslijepodne, a planinarenje ujutro — odlučuje se za planinarenje.

qs.q: You hear Barbara talking about her new apartment. What does Barbara say about it?
qs.exp: Barbara hvali lokaciju: prodavaonice, tržnica, dobra autobusna linija. Kaže da je “just big enough” (nije velika) i svjesno su platili više za lokaciju.

qs.q: You hear a scientist talking. What is the main topic of the discussion?
qs.exp: Znanstvenik govori o porastu temperatura i efektu staklenika → globalno zatopljenje (global warming) je glavna tema, ašuma i zagađenje su uzroci.

qs.q: You hear Jenny talking about her exam next week. How does she feel about it?
qs.exp: Jenny kaže: “you never know what might come up” i opisuje noćnu moru o ispitu. Unatoč pripremi, nije sigurna → nervozna (nervous).

qs.q: You hear Bob talking about his summer job. Why did he do it?
qs.exp: “I’ve got a friend who sells jewellery... and he asked me to help him out.” → zbog prijatelja (for a friend).

qs.q: You hear Susan talking about a book. What does Susan think of it?
qs.exp: Susan kaže: “it’s fascinating to learn about how they built these cathedrals and how people lived at the time” → informativna (informative). Duga je, ali to je karakteristika, ne njeno mišljenje o njoj.

qs.q: You hear a teacher talking to a student about his essay. What is the problem with the essay?
qs.exp: Nastavnik: “I read a sentence and I wonder what it’s got to do with the previous one... you obviously wrote it without planning it.” → organizacija (organisation).

qs.q:
You hear a conversation about buying a book for a friend Isabella.
For each question (14–19), decide which book it refers to:
A = Angelica, B = Bounder, C = Cluster
items: 15 has been made into a film?

pairs.l: 15 has been made into a film?

qs.exp: Bounder: SF (“set in a distant galaxy”), skup (hardback), duga knjiga. Angelica: film adaptacija (“she might have seen it at the cinema”), bestseller (najpopularnija). Cluster: prijevod (“won awards in Spanish and English”), kratka (“only a couple of hundred pages”).

qs.q: Which book has been made into a film?
qs.exp: “She might have seen it at the cinema” → Angelica je ekranizirana.

qs.q: Which book is a translation?
qs.exp: “Won literary awards both in the original Spanish and in English.” → Cluster je prevođena knjiga.

qs.q: Which book is the most popular?
qs.exp: “It’s on the best-seller list” → Angelica je najpopularnija.

qs.q: Which book is the shortest?
qs.exp: “It’s only a couple of hundred pages long” → Cluster je najkraća.

qs.q: Which book is the most expensive?
qs.exp: “It’s in hardback. It’s not in paperback yet. The other two are paperback and are half the price.” → Bounder je najskuplji.

qs.q: What does the reviewer say about the show’s format?
qs.exp: “Like any show that becomes hugely successful, it has a familiar format. The viewers know what to expect.” → predvidljiv (predictable).

qs.q: The show is a success because of its…
qs.exp: “The magic ingredient, however, which sets the show apart... came when it was handed over to Brian Woolley.” → voditelj (presenter).

qs.q: The show is broadcast live…
qs.exp: “It’s come a long way since it was broadcast on Saturday afternoons... So it’s no wonder it was switched to the evening.” → sada se emitira navečer.

qs.q: Brian Woolley is…
qs.exp: “Although born and raised in far-off Australia...” → Australac.

qs.q: Woolley’s book is about…
qs.exp: “The book focuses on the basics of English cooking, bringing you back to the traditional Sunday meals.” → engleska hrana.

qs.q: Woolley plans to…
qs.exp: “There’s good news for fans of Home Cooking. Brian’s already got his list of celebrity guests.” → novi serijal (another series).

qs.q:
Laptops instead of textbooks — Which person thinks that…

A=Annabelle (textbooks should remain, highlight with pen, laptops cause injuries and addiction)
B=Bradley (laptops as supplements, not replacement; parents should insure school laptops; laptops have limits e.g. power cuts)
C=Cheryl (reduce back injuries but kids misuse laptops; teachers rarely use laptops; everyone learns differently)
D=Dominic (digital revolution cannot be turned back; parents should purchase their own laptops; teachers need training)
E=Elaine (information changes quickly; students not mature enough; tools to minimise distractions; online homework reduces socialising)
F=Forrest (kids hate hauling textbooks; cost of maintaining networks cancels benefits; sometimes textbook is quicker)

0. students often damage their laptops? [C=Cheryl]
1. laptops should be used as an additional learning tool?
2. getting rid of textbooks would change teaching methods?
3. despite being heavy, textbooks are still useful?
4. the budget for laptop maintenance is bigger than for textbooks?
5. too much time on laptops can cause health issues?
6. children will need help to stay focused while working with laptops?
7. the use of laptops could result in withdrawal from peers?
8. the traditional approach to learning will die out?
9. finding information in a textbook can be quicker than on a laptop?
10. getting rid of textbooks would disadvantage some students?
11. students should own their laptops?
12. you cannot always depend on laptops?
items: 1 — laptops should be used as an additional learning tool?
2 — getting rid of textbooks would change teaching methods?
3 — despite being heavy, textbooks are still useful?
4 — the budget for laptop maintenance is bigger than for textbooks?
5 — too much time on laptops can cause health issues?
6 — children will need help to stay focused while working with laptops?
7 — the use of laptops could result in withdrawal from peers?
8 — the traditional approach to learning will die out?
9 — finding information in a textbook can be quicker than on a laptop?
10 — getting rid of textbooks would disadvantage some students?
12 — you cannot always depend on laptops?

pairs.l: 1 — laptops should be used as an additional learning tool?
2 — getting rid of textbooks would change teaching methods?
3 — despite being heavy, textbooks are still useful?
4 — the budget for laptop maintenance is bigger than for textbooks?
5 — too much time on laptops can cause health issues?
6 — children will need help to stay focused while working with laptops?
7 — the use of laptops could result in withdrawal from peers?
8 — the traditional approach to learning will die out?
9 — finding information in a textbook can be quicker than on a laptop?
10 — getting rid of textbooks would disadvantage some students?
12 — you cannot always depend on laptops?

qs.exp: 1=B (Bradley: 'laptops would make wonderful SUPPLEMENTS'). 2=D (Dominic: 'Education will IRREVOCABLY CHANGE... teachers will need FURTHER TRAINING'). 3=F (Forrest: 'they may well have a point even if they are generally written to match the students' reading ability'). 4=F (Forrest: 'the benefits of quick updates are CANCELLED OUT by the cost of maintaining networks'). 5=A (Annabelle: 'students overusing them can result in various types of INJURIES... withdrawal symptoms'). 6=E (Elaine: 'some tools should be used to MINIMISE students' attention being DIVERTED by online distractions'). 7=E (Elaine: 'online homework might REDUCE THE NEED TO SOCIALISE with classmates'). 8=D (Dominic: 'This digital revolution... CANNOT BE TURNED BACK'). 9=F (Forrest: 'sometimes it is a lot simpler than logging on, searching for the appropriate link'). 10=C (Cheryl: 'tossing books away would help one group of students while HINDERING ANOTHER'). 11=D (Dominic: 'the parents should be the ones to PURCHASE them'). 12=B (Bradley: 'laptops have their limits, such as when there is a POWER CUT, while a BOOK CAN ALWAYS BE OPENED').

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"I am, and always have been, a BIBLIOPHILE, with broad tastes."

What does the author say in the first paragraph?
A She likes books.
B Social media bore her.
C She doesn't like wasting money.
D She is an intellectual.
qs.exp: 'I am, and always have been, a BIBLIOPHILE' = ljubiteljica knjiga = A.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"I studiously read the promotional descriptions on their jacket covers, and thumb through them, HOPING THAT OTHER BROWSERS WILL APPRECIATE HOW CLEVER I AM."

Why does the author begin browsing serious books?
A She likes the complicated storylines.
B She is fond of hardbacks.
C She enjoys reading the jackets.
D She wants to look smart.
qs.exp: 'Hoping that other browsers will appreciate HOW CLEVER I AM' = želi izgledati pametno = D.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"You can be exposed to suffering and heartache, but they don't belong to you, they are someone else's pain. And you know that, DESPITE THE OBSTACLES, LOVE WILL WIN OUT."

Why does the author like romantic novels?
A They are better than friends.
B They always have a happy ending.
C They make you feel heartache.
D They can be shocking.
opts: They always have a happy ending.
qs.exp: 'Despite the obstacles, LOVE WILL WIN OUT' = uvijek sretni kraj = B.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"I am a big fan of ESCAPISM. No matter how difficult our own lives might be, a GOOD STORY CAN PUSH ALL OUR TROUBLES AWAY."

What does the author think about the effects of romantic fiction?
A They are equally good and bad.
B Reading romantic fiction can be dangerous.
C Escapism helps us put up with our lives.
D Romantic novels can help you find love.
opts: They are equally good and bad.
Reading romantic fiction can be dangerous.
Escapism helps us put up with our lives.
Romantic novels can help you find love.
qs.exp: 'I am a big fan of escapism... a good story can PUSH ALL OUR TROUBLES AWAY' = eskapizam pomaže podnijeti život = C.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"Most important for me is that the characters are easy for us to IDENTIFY WITH. We want to be able to RELATE with what happens to them, which SHOULD REFLECT OUR OWN LIVES."

What does the author say about the characters in romantic novels?
A They should have ordinary experiences.
B They should possess strong identities.
C They should keep journals.
D They should include some sensible men.
opts: They should include some sensible men.
qs.exp: 'What happens to them should REFLECT OUR OWN LIVES' = trebaju imati obična, prepoznatljiva iskustva = A.

qs.q:
Romantic Fiction

"Reading romantic fiction is the equivalent of EATING A BOWL OF YOUR FAVOURITE POTATO CHIPS while watching your favourite programme. It might not be NUTRITIOUS but a part of you CANNOT RESIST IT."

According to the author, why is romantic fiction popular with women?
A It is reassuringly familiar.
B It is a pleasurable experience.
C They like the male heroes.
D They don't want to think too hard.
opts: They don't want to think too hard.
qs.exp: 'Like eating favourite potato chips... a part of you cannot resist it' = ugodno iskustvo = B.

qs.q:
Manchester – a city never lost for words

"Linguists at the University of Manchester have discovered their city has a population that speaks at least 153 languages. (19) ____. Research conducted by professor Yaron Matras suggests the true figure could be even higher."

A This has consequently prompted concerns about assimilation.
B The most important ones are immigration and the arrival of overseas students to the city.
C It may have substantially underestimated the number of multilingual households across the UK.
D However, it is still less diverse than Manchester as it tends to have very established communities.
E It could have helped to forge the city's linguistic and cultural diversity.
F This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places linguistically.
G It is much more active in responding to language needs at the level of public services.
H This huge ratio indicates just how deeply rooted and firmly established its linguistic culture is.
opts: A — This prompted concerns about assimilation.
B — The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C — It may have underestimated the number of multilingual households.
D — Still less diverse than Manchester.
E — It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F — This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places linguistically.
G — It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H — This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
qs.exp: 'Population speaks at least 153 languages. (19)____. The true figure could be even higher.' → F: This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places linguistically.

qs.q:
Manchester

"Manchester's language diversity is higher than many countries'. This is very likely to put it on top of the list in Europe due to many factors. (20) ____. As they continue flowing in, it's fair to say that this already large list is set to grow."

A This has prompted concerns about assimilation.
B The most important ones are immigration and the arrival of overseas students to the city.
C It may have underestimated the number of multilingual households.
D However, it is still less diverse than Manchester.
E It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
opts: A — This prompted concerns about assimilation.
B — The most important ones are immigration and the arrival of overseas students to the city.
C — It may have underestimated multilingual households.
D — Still less diverse than Manchester.
E — It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F — This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G — It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H — This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
qs.exp: 'On top of the list due to many factors. (20)____. As THEY continue flowing in, list set to grow.' → B: The most important ones are immigration and the arrival of overseas students to the city. 'They' = immigrants/students.

qs.q:
Manchester

"Around two-thirds of Mancunian schoolchildren are bilingual. (21) ____. And there are also some rare languages spoken in the city: Chitrali, Konkani, Dagaare, and Uyghur."

A This has prompted concerns about assimilation.
B The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C It may have underestimated multilingual households.
D However, it is still less diverse than Manchester.
E It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H This huge ratio indicates just how deeply rooted and firmly established its linguistic culture is.
opts: A — This prompted concerns about assimilation.
B — The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C — It may have underestimated multilingual households.
D — Still less diverse than Manchester.
E — It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F — This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G — It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H — This huge ratio indicates just how deeply rooted and firmly established its linguistic culture is.
qs.exp: 'Two-thirds of schoolchildren are bilingual. (21)____. And there are rare languages.' → H: This HUGE RATIO indicates just how DEEPLY ROOTED and FIRMLY ESTABLISHED its linguistic culture is.

qs.q:
Manchester

"Melbourne, for example, is famous for its many languages. (22) ____. New York, on the other hand, is significantly larger in size and has been attracting immigrants for as long as Manchester."

A This has prompted concerns about assimilation.
B The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C It may have underestimated multilingual households.
D However, it is still less diverse than Manchester as it tends to have very established communities.
E It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
opts: A — This prompted concerns about assimilation.
B — The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C — It may have underestimated multilingual households.
D — However, it is still less diverse than Manchester as it tends to have very established communities.
E — It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F — This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G — It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H — This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
qs.exp: 'Melbourne is famous for its many languages. (22)____. New York is larger and has attracted immigrants just as long.' → D: However, it is still LESS DIVERSE than Manchester as it tends to have very ESTABLISHED COMMUNITIES.

qs.q:
Manchester

"The past decade has seen a very noticeable change in the population of England and Wales, with the foreign-born population increasing. (23) ____. Labour's leader, Ed Miliband, said everyone in Britain should know how to speak English."

A This has consequently prompted concerns about assimilation.
B The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C It may have underestimated multilingual households.
D However, it is still less diverse than Manchester.
E It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
opts: A — This has consequently prompted concerns about assimilation.
B — The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C — It may have underestimated multilingual households.
D — Still less diverse than Manchester.
E — It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F — This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G — It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H — This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
qs.exp: 'Foreign-born population increasing. (23)____. Miliband said everyone should speak English.' → A: This has consequently PROMPTED CONCERNS about ASSIMILATION.

qs.q:
Manchester

"Matras's research suggests something else about the census. (24) ____. And it is still growing."

A This has prompted concerns about assimilation.
B The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C It may have substantially underestimated the number of multilingual households across the UK.
D However, it is still less diverse than Manchester.
E It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
opts: A — This has prompted concerns about assimilation.
B — The most important ones are immigration and overseas students.
C — It may have substantially underestimated the number of multilingual households across the UK.
D — Still less diverse than Manchester.
E — It could have helped forge the city's linguistic diversity.
F — This fact makes it one of the world's most diverse places.
G — It is much more active in responding to language needs.
H — This huge ratio indicates how deeply rooted its linguistic culture is.
qs.exp: 'Matras's research suggests something else about the census. (24)____. And it is still growing.' → C: It may have substantially UNDERESTIMATED the number of multilingual households across the UK.

qs.q:
Columbo

"This disarmingly polite homicide detective seemed to chomp on the same short cigar on a (25) ____ basis."

A day after day
B day by day
C day
D daily
qs.exp: 'On a DAILY basis' — fiksna kolokacija: on a daily basis = svakodnevno.

qs.q:
Columbo

"His hair was always messy. (26) ____, beneath this faintly comical exterior was probably the most dogged investigator."

A However
B Indeed
C Furthermore
D Despite
qs.exp: 'Hair messy and comical. HOWEVER, beneath this was the most dogged investigator.' — 'however' za kontrast.

qs.q:
Columbo

"Columbo was often (27) ____ on to investigate high profile murders."

A put
B asked
C called
D told
qs.exp: 'Was often CALLED ON to investigate' — frazalni glagol: call on = pozvati, angažirati nekoga.

qs.q:
Columbo

"His trademark was to tell them he was done, then he (28) ____ move towards the door, turn back and say, 'Oh, just one last question'."

A should
B would
C could
D will
qs.exp: 'He WOULD move towards the door' — 'would' za uobičajenu prošlu radnju (habitually did).

qs.q:
Columbo

"That's the question they were sure he wouldn't (29) ____."

A be asking
B have been asking
C be asked
D have been asked
qs.exp: 'They were sure he wouldn't BE ASKING' — wouldn't + be asking (negative future continuous za nešto što ne očekuju da će se postaviti).

qs.q:
Columbo

"They go from being certain they'll (30) ____ away with their crime to knowing they've been caught!"

A go
B come
C turn
D get
qs.exp: 'They'll GET AWAY with their crime' — frazalni glagol: get away with = proći nekažnjeno.

qs.q:
Columbo

"Lieutenant Columbo's wife (31) ____ a very important role but she was never seen."

A did
B acted
C played
D made
qs.exp: 'His wife PLAYED a very important role' — fiksna kolokacija: play a role = igrati ulogu.

qs.q:
Columbo

"Columbo was always talking about things his wife (32) ____ told him or what little chore she wanted him to do."

A had
B has
C have
D having
qs.exp: 'Things his wife HAD told him' — past perfect u indirektnom govoru (pluperfect za radnju u daljnjoj prošlosti).

qs.q:
Seed Bank

"It contains 4.5 million different seed samples ensuring that bio diverse plant life can be restored in the event (33) ____ a great natural disaster."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'In the event OF a great natural disaster' — fiksni izraz: in the event of = u slučaju.

qs.q:
Seed Bank

"The vault is secured against most threats, even extremely drastic ones (34) ____ as asteroids and nuclear bombs."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Drastic ones SUCH as asteroids' — fiksni izraz: such as = poput, na primjer.

qs.q:
Seed Bank

"The temperature here never exceeds minus four degrees Celsius (35) ____ if there's a power cut."

(Upiši jednu ili dvije riječi — više prihvatljivih odgovora)
qs.exp: 'Never exceeds minus four EVEN if there's a power cut' — 'even if' = čak i ako; ili 'except if' = osim ako.

qs.q:
Seed Bank

"Power cuts (36) ____ actually occur some time ago when rainwater from a storm made its way into a transformer."

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Power cuts DID actually occur' — 'did' za naglasak/emfazu u pozitivnoj rečenici (emphasising that it really happened).

qs.q:
Seed Bank

qs.q:
Why do some people learn faster?

"The first reaction appears immediately after a mistake and is the inevitable response to any lapse. (19) ____. It occurs when we pay attention to the error, dwelling on the disappointing result."

A Simply commending someone for 'being' smart stimulates the wish to 'look' smart.
B This meant that the experience of failure had been so discouraging that instead of improving, they regressed.
C The second signal arrives later and is associated with awareness.
D This inevitably implies that the extra awareness always pays dividends in performance.
E However, it induces frequent mistakes, as the boring procedure encourages people to zone out.
F Education is neither magic nor is it the wisdom derived from failure.
G The other has a growth mind-set and they believe that we can get better at almost anything.
H Unless we experience the unpleasant symptoms of being wrong, our mind will never revise its models.
opts: A — Being commended for being smart stimulates the wish to look smart.
B — The experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.
C — The second signal arrives later and is associated with awareness.
D — Extra awareness always pays dividends in performance.
E — It induces frequent mistakes as the boring procedure encourages people to zone out.
F — Education is neither magic nor wisdom derived from failure.
G — The other has a growth mind-set and believes we can get better.
H — Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.
qs.exp: 'The FIRST reaction... inevitable response to lapse. (19)____. It occurs when we PAY ATTENTION to the error.' → C: The SECOND signal arrives later and is associated with AWARENESS.

qs.q:
Why do some people learn faster?

"One group has a fixed mind-set and tends to agree: 'You cannot do much to change your intelligence.' (20) ____. While the first see mistakes as a dismal failure, the second look at them as the engine of education."

A Simply commending someone for 'being' smart stimulates the wish to 'look' smart.
B This meant the experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.

F Education is neither magic nor wisdom.

H Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.
opts: A — Being commended for being smart stimulates the wish to look smart.
B — The experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.
C — The second signal arrives later.
D — Extra awareness always pays dividends.
F — Education is neither magic nor wisdom.
G — The other has a growth mind-set and believes we can get better at almost anything, provided we invest time and energy.
H — Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.
qs.exp: 'Fixed mind-set: can't change intelligence. (20)____. First see mistakes as failure, second as engine of education.' → G: The other has a GROWTH mind-set and they believe that we can get better at almost anything.

qs.q:
Why do some people learn faster?

"The experiment begins with identifying the middle letter of a five-letter series – quite a simple change. (21) ____. Once they make a mistake, of course, they immediately regret it."

A Simply commending someone for 'being' smart stimulates the wish to 'look' smart.

E However, it induces frequent mistakes, as the boring procedure encourages people to zone out.

H Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.

qs.q:
Why do some people learn faster?

"Those with a growth mind-set are significantly better at learning from their mistakes. Increased attention to their mistakes is correlated with improvement after the error. (22) ____. Because the subjects are thinking about what they got wrong, they learn how to get it right."

A Simply commending for 'being' smart stimulates the wish to 'look' smart.
B The experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.
C The second signal arrives later.
D This inevitably implies that the extra awareness always pays dividends in performance.
E It induces frequent mistakes.
F Education is neither magic nor wisdom.
G The other has a growth mind-set.
H Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.
opts: A — Being commended for being smart stimulates the wish to look smart.
B — The experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.
C — The second signal arrives later.
D — This inevitably implies that the extra awareness always pays dividends in performance.
F — Education is neither magic nor wisdom.
G — The other has a growth mind-set.
H — Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.
qs.exp: 'Increased attention correlated with improvement. (22)____. Thinking about what they got wrong → learn how to get it right.' → D: This inevitably implies that the extra awareness always pays dividends in performance.

qs.q:
Why do some people learn faster?

"Praising also plays two different roles in learning success. (23) ____. This fear of failure encourages them to avoid learning from their mistakes."

B The experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.
C The second signal arrives later.
D Extra awareness always pays dividends.
E It induces frequent mistakes.

B — The experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.
C — The second signal arrives later.
D — Extra awareness always pays dividends.
F — Education is neither magic nor wisdom.
G — The other has a growth mind-set.
H — Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.

qs.q:

"Making a mistake causes embarrassment, but it is an irreplaceable component of learning. (24) ____. It will keep on making the same mistakes, forsaking self-improvement for the sake of self-confidence."

D — Extra awareness always pays dividends.

G — The other has a growth mind-set.
H — Unless we experience the unpleasant symptoms of being wrong, our mind will never revise its models.
qs.exp: 'Making mistakes is irreplaceable component of learning. (24)____. It will keep making the same mistakes.' → H: Unless we experience the unpleasant symptoms of being wrong, our mind will never revise its models.

The porcupine's prickly defence

(Upiši jednu ili dvije riječi — više prihvatljivih odgovora)

The porcupine's prickly defence

qs.q:

(Upiši jednu riječ)

qs.q:

qs.exp: 'IN conjunction with the claws' — fiksni izraz: in conjunction with = zajedno s, u kombinaciji s.

The airport was too crowded with English tourists.

The designer clothes his female companions are wearing.

Eating the same meat soup as the dogs.

qs.q:

"We worry too much about what people around us think of us. (19) ____. Everyone around you has an opinion, but in reality, others' opinions are based more on their history than anything you're actually doing."

B If it does not bring you happiness, it will, at worst, help you be miserable in comfort.
C That is more than a fine stretch to fit a whole host of wonderful endeavours into your life.
D If you waste too much time seeking validation, respect or approval from them, you won't have time to accomplish all that you desire.
E Consequently, such thoughts serve the purpose of knocking down the obstacles in your way.
F Evidently, dishonesty, disrespect, unhappiness and evil exist and you will have to deal with them.
G This goes to say that you can't influence unmet expectations, bygone situations and failures.
H Nor does it insulate you from pain, suffering and conflict.

H — Nor does it insulate you from pain and conflict.

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"The ice sheets would raise sea levels by 65 metres if they (25) ____ completely."

A would melt
B had melted
C melt
D melted
qs.exp: 'Would raise sea levels IF THEY MELTED completely' — uvjetna rečenica 2. tipa: if + past simple → would. 'If they melted' (nerealni uvjet).

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"A survey (26) ____ that most glaciologists believe melting could be more rapid."

A found
B resulted
C pointed
D told
qs.exp: 'A survey FOUND that...' — 'find' uz 'that' = otkriti, pokazati (rezultati istraživanja).

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"Melting would raise the average global sea level by 29 cm in this century (27) ____."

A only
B alone
C sole
D apart
qs.exp: '29 cm in this century ALONE' — 'alone' uz imenice/fraze = samo, isključivo (29 cm, and that's just for this century).

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"There is a chance of it increasing even (28) ____ by a catastrophic 84 cm."

A farther
B further
C adding
D added
qs.exp: 'Increasing even FURTHER by 84 cm' — 'further' za apstraktno povećanje (more, beyond that).

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"This would take the total sea-level increase to (29) ____ over 100 centimetres."

A good
B near
C well
D close
qs.exp: 'Take the total to WELL OVER 100 centimetres' — 'well over' = znatno više od, dobrano iznad.

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"The impact of a metre rise in (30) ____ sea level would potentially be severe."

A a
B the
C some
D any
qs.exp: 'A rise in THE sea level' — određeni član 'the' uz 'sea level' (jedinstven, opće poznat pojam).

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"A warmer world not only causes oceans to expand thermally (31) ____ additionally leads to faster melting."

A and
B but
C still
D yet
qs.exp: 'Not only... BUT additionally' — fiksni izraz: not only... but (also) = ne samo... nego i.

qs.q:
A wrong calculation?

"Glaciologists are uncertain about how the ice sheets will respond (32) ____ increasing global temperatures."

A with
B in
C by
D to
qs.exp: 'Respond TO increasing global temperatures' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: respond to = reagirati na.

(Upiši jednu ili dvije riječi — više prihvatljivih odgovora)

qs.q:

qs.q:

(Upiši jednu riječ)
qs.exp: 'Not brave ENOUGH to leave their homes' — 'enough' iza pridjeva: adj + enough + to-infinitive.

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that advertising has a negative influence on our lifestyle. Others say advertising is a useful service."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA negativan utjecaj: potiče konzumerizam, nezdrave životne navike (brza hrana), nerealna tijela, manipulacija. ZA korisnu uslugu: informira o proizvodima, potiče ekonomiju, besplatni mediji. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:

A — Their coach.
B — Their mother.
C — Their sibling.
D — Their teacher.
E — Their relative.
F — Their favourite novelist.
G — Their favourite neighbour.
H — Their favourite celebrity.
qs.exp: Prema ključu: 1=B, 2=A, 3=D, 4=F, 5=G.

What did they get Molly?

Rejecting the invitation for a meal.
Talking about a meal he has just had.

How did she feel at the performance?

Why does she have to interview the old man again?

The old man fell asleep during the interview.

What does the man say about the beach?
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q10 = C (It's child-friendly).

You hear a radio announcer talking about local government.
What is she doing?
opts: Telling somebody to stop doing something.
Praising somebody for having done something.

qs.q:
You hear a piece of radio news.
Why was the company in court?
opts: Because they had sent spam messages.
Because they had violated customers' privacy.
Because their offer was found to be deceptive.

You hear a radio report on a real-estate market survey.
What did the survey show?
opts: There's a difference in house prices between London boroughs.
Real-estate prices in London are without comparison.

Decide which neighbourhood (A–C) each question (14–19) refers to.

A = Applewood
B = Brentwood
C = Collingwood

Which neighbourhood…
items: 16 — offers a variety of social life?

pairs.l: 16 — offers a variety of social life?

qs.exp: Prema ključu: 14=C, 15=B, 16=C, 17=B, 18=A, 19=A.

qs.q:
You hear a radio interview with Lizzie Armitstead, a cycling champion.

What does she like best about her success?
opts: The fact that she won silver.
The way she entered the finish.
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q20 = C (The self-confidence she found).

qs.q: Why did Lizzie start cycling?
opts: She was always attracted to sports outfits.
She was impressed by the racing atmosphere.
She wanted to overcome her childish fears.
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q21 = B (She was impressed by the racing atmosphere).

opts: The lack of focus at the beginning of the race.
Going on instinct at the very finish.
Thinking about the medal before the finish.

qs.q: What does she like about cycling?
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q23 = A (The challenge).

qs.q: What does she find difficult about being a professional?
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q24 = A (Being away from family).

qs.q: What does Lizzie think about being a celebrity?
qs.exp: Prema ključu: Q25 = C (She thinks it's a nuisance).

qs.q:
Language Teachers — Which person had a language teacher who…

A=Aaron (French teacher taught entirely in French, even beginners, came Saturdays, Aaron became fluent)
B=Brigitte (English teacher: positive feedback, subtle corrections, varied methods, word dominos/charades as rewards)
C=Carl (Spanish teacher: fun methods, pirate dress-up, treasure hunt, abandoned classroom, then went abroad)
D=Daphne (Russian teacher: personal, joined games, sat with groups, visits/excursions, never native language in class)
E=Ella (Italian teacher from university, wanted success but confusing worksheets, students dozed off, gave sweets for book reports)
F=Frank (German teacher, former sociologist, focused on mistakes not progress, made him hate German)

0. took part in games? [D=Daphne]
1. taught another subject at their school?
2. never spoke their native language in class?
3. preferred traditional teaching methods?
4. enjoyed teaching grammar?
5. introduced games as a reward?
6. organised extra lessons for them?
7. encouraged them to read literature?
8. concentrated on correcting errors?
9. took them on field trips?
10. taught them to speak fluently?
11. had no previous teaching experience?
12. left to teach abroad?
items: 1 — taught another subject at their school?
2 — never spoke their native language in class?

pairs.l: 1 — taught another subject at their school?
2 — never spoke their native language in class?

qs.exp: 1=B (Brigitte: 'we heard she was a DIFFERENT PERSON when she taught Italian' = predavala drugi predmet). 2=A (Aaron: teacher taught entirely in French, 'we never spoke our native language in front of him' applies to D, but A: 'taught our class entirely in French WITHOUT EXCEPTION'). 3=F (Frank: 'German grammar MUST BE TAUGHT THE OLD WAY'). 4=F (Frank: 'we'd discuss adjective agreement and many other things'). 5=B (Brigitte: 'if we'd completed our work successfully, she'd let us do word dominos or charades'). 6=A (Aaron: 'would even come in on SATURDAYS to work with us'). 7=E (Ella: 'give us sweets if we chose a BOOK on our own and handed in a REPORT'). 8=F (Frank: 'teacher emphasised MY MISTAKES rather than focusing on my progress'). 9=D (Daphne: 'we'd visit an exhibition occasionally, or go collect plants'). 10=A (Aaron: 'when I later became FLUENT in French, I knew I had mostly him to thank'). 11=E (Ella: 'obviously, she didn't have a clue about TEACHING HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS' = previously taught university). 12=C (Carl: 'he entered a FOREIGN EXCHANGE PROGRAMME FOR TEACHERS').

"'My shoe sponsors would kill me if I was pictured without them.'"

Farah is wearing high heels because…
A she feels short without them.
B it fits her image.
C she has to wear them.
D she likes them.
qs.exp: 'My shoe SPONSORS WOULD KILL ME if I was pictured without them' = obveza prema sponzorima = C (she has to wear them).

Farah Frill

opts: as a result of a previous role.

Farah Frill

"The part is far from the brainless blonde teen of some years ago but CLOSE TO MY BROADWAY VENTURES."

Farah's new role…
A is similar to her recent work.
B is a part of a new Broadway show.
C shocked her.
D is humorous.
opts: is similar to her recent work.
is a part of a new Broadway show.

qs.q:
Farah Frill

"I think HER PERFORMANCE STANDS ABOVE that of the other nominees, and I would be DISAPPOINTED if she didn't win."

The author thinks that Farah…
A should have won an Oscar.

The author thinks that the aim of the Oscars should be…
A to market the selected films.
B to reflect cinematic quality.
C to provide awards for the in-crowd.

The author says that Obsession is…
A historical fact.
B a romantic comedy.
C a psychological drama.
D an action film.
qs.exp: 'The only question: whether it is too FANCIFUL. Characters are based on real characters... passionate, driven, forever in conflict.' = psihološka drama = C.

qs.q:
Want to be a Wimbledon ballboy?

"I look distinctly out of place in the warm-up. (0=I). But mostly because these teenagers show no visible signs of exhaustion, whereas I'm completely sweaty. In my defence, this is a well-drilled squad of super-teens. (19) ___. Almost all of them will be ballboys and ballgirls at this week's Wimbledon."

A All training sessions begin with the standard warm-up: a circuit of fitness exercises that I, apparently, can't do.
B This is tougher than it sounds: I was bending a knee and fidgeting within 30 seconds.
C Those who pass go on to train in simulated matches.
D She tells me she was once hit by a ball at over 100mph.
E They are among the survivors of a rigorous process that has reduced around 1,000 applicants to an elite core of 250.
F The result is a chance to get close to sporting royalty.
G It is not enough just to get the ball where it needs to be.
H If a BBG makes a mistake, the result is almost always disastrously high-profile.
opts: A — Training begins with fitness exercises I apparently can't do.
B — Tougher than it sounds — fidgeting within 30 seconds.
C — Those who pass go on to train in simulated matches.
D — She was once hit by a ball at over 100mph.
E — Survivors of a rigorous process: 1,000 applicants reduced to 250.
F — The result is a chance to get close to sporting royalty.
G — It is not enough just to get the ball where it needs to be.
H — If a BBG makes a mistake, it's disastrously high-profile.
qs.exp: 'Well-drilled squad of super-teens. (19)___. Almost all will be BBGs at Wimbledon.' → E: They are among the survivors of a rigorous process that has reduced around 1,000 applicants to an elite core of 250.

qs.q:
High school reunion — Which person…

A=Adam (saw photos, ex missed reunion, moved to Australia due to job shortage, wants to stay in touch)
B=Benjamin (entered hall, couldn't recognise anyone, wanted to leave, wife Linda stopped him, still together)
C=Conrad (flew in from Stockholm business meeting, late, disappointed — felt like strangers, never again)
D=Danielle (almost didn't come, short time, husband, surprised to see Jessica, left first)
E=Ethan (was bullied/nerd, met them again, surprisingly immature, doesn't bear grudges, wonders if they're happy)
F=Francesca (unsure whether to go, two weeks choosing outfit, unemployed, uncomfortable, endured it)

0. was an excellent student? [E=Ethan: 'was considered a nerd']
1. is unemployed?
2. is a successful businessman?
3. thinks nothing has changed?
4. left early?
5. wouldn't like to see their classmates again?
6. lives abroad?
7. didn't feel good about their appearance?
8. married their high school sweetheart?
9. did not recognise almost anybody?
10. was disappointed?
11. was pleasantly surprised?
12. wasn't at the reunion?
items: 5 — wouldn't like to see their classmates again?
7 — didn't feel good about their appearance?

pairs.l: 5 — wouldn't like to see their classmates again?
7 — didn't feel good about their appearance?

qs.exp: 1=F (Francesca: 'being without work, I rarely buy fancy clothes'). 2=C (Conrad: 'negotiate the takeover of a large pharmaceutical company'). 3=E (Ethan: 'The way they behaved was surprisingly IMMATURE. As if there hadn't been a 15-year gap'). 4=D (Danielle: 'we were the FIRST TO GO'). 5=C (Conrad: 'One thing is sure, I'll NEVER GO TO A REUNION AGAIN'). 6=A (Adam: 'now that I have moved to Australia'). 7=F (Francesca: 'two weeks to decide what I would wear... hide those 10 extra kilos'). 8=B (Benjamin: 'Linda, my wife... Even during our school days she was more reasonable than me'). 9=B (Benjamin: 'I couldn't put the faces and the names together... I wanted to leave straightaway'). 10=C (Conrad: 'I had a feeling I was among strangers. We had nothing to say to each other'). 11=D (Danielle: "I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw my best school friend, Jessica"). 12=A (Adam: 'I've seen all the PHOTOGRAPHS... I wish I'd been there').

Today's kids JUST IGNORE them'). 3=E (Esther: 'Families need to learn to CONTROL OUR USE OF TECHNOLOGY'). 4=F (Fiona: 'YouTube is fantastic, computer games great fun'). 5=C (Catherine: 'I SOMETIMES WONDER'). 6=D (David: 'OBESITY is also a fast growing problem'). 7=B (Brian: 'Machines help with tasks that TOOK UP HOURS'). 8=C (Catherine: 'The family is physically together, but ARE THEY PAYING ATTENTION TO EACH OTHER?'). 9=D (David: 'Home entertainment is so much better that families are MORE LIKELY TO SPEND TIME TOGETHER'). 10=E (Esther: 'It's like we've got super-advanced new toys and WE DON'T YET KNOW HOW TO PLAY WITH THEM'). 11=D (David: 'on the whole I think technology is GOOD FOR US'). 12=F (Fiona: 'CYBERSPACE CAN BE A RISKY PLACE, you never know who you're talking to, and CYBER-BULLYING is horrible').

Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that testing in school should be limited to final exams. Others say tests should be given as often as possible."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA samo završne ispite: manje stresa, više vremena za učenje, fokus na razumijevanje. ZA česte testove: praćenje napretka, motivacija, bolja priprema za završne. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:
Handwriting

H Instead, the relationship between handwriting and personality has been firmly established.

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people think that having a university degree is essential for a successful career. Others disagree."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA fakultetsku diplomu: bolji prihodi, više mogućnosti zapošljavanja, razvoj vještina, prestiž. PROTIV: praktično iskustvo vrijedi više, skupo, nije potrebno u svim karijerama, samouki uspjeh. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:

they will want to share with us.

humans are predicted to lack empathy.
only particular skills will be required.
humans will have too much time on their hands.

the development of Ems depends largely on brain scanning.
artificial intelligence is hard to predict.

qs.q:
The Lost Language of Easter Island

"Only limited information has been gathered from Rapanui people, and most of it still cannot be identified. (23) ______. Researchers have announced an algorithm that could automatically decipher a lost language."

A Academics disagree about when the writing system emerged.
B Claims to have deciphered rongorongo tablets have been confirmed by other linguists.
C However, these signs are merely symbolic prompts.
D It is covered with rows of stylized signs, so called glyphs.
E For the locals they are a source of great admiration.
F This is mainly so due to the lack of artefacts.
G It appears religious rituals were used for that.
H But there are hopes machine learning could help in the future.
opts: A — Academics disagree about when the writing system emerged.
B — Claims to have deciphered tablets have been confirmed by linguists.
C — However, these signs are merely symbolic prompts.
D — It is covered with rows of stylized signs, so called glyphs.
E — For the locals they are a source of great admiration.
F — This is mainly so due to the lack of artefacts.
G — It appears religious rituals were used for that.
H — But there are hopes machine learning could help in the future.
qs.exp: 'Limited information, most cannot be identified. (23)______. Researchers have announced an algorithm to decipher a lost language.' → H: But there are HOPES MACHINE LEARNING COULD HELP in the future.

qs.q:
The Lost Language of Easter Island

"The indecipherable glyphs still generate significant pride on the island, as well as intrigue. (24) ______. On the other hand, the script is as much a mystery for them as for the rest of the world."

A Academics disagree about when the writing system emerged.
B Claims to have deciphered rongorongo tablets have been confirmed by other linguists.
C However, these signs are merely symbolic prompts.
D It is covered with rows of stylized signs, so called glyphs.
E For the locals they are a source of great admiration and awe towards their ancestors.
F This is mainly so due to the lack of artefacts.
G It appears religious rituals were used for that.
H But there are hopes machine learning could help in the future.
opts: A — Academics disagree about when the writing system emerged.
B — Claims to have deciphered tablets have been confirmed by linguists.
C — However, these signs are merely symbolic prompts.
D — It is covered with rows of stylized signs, so called glyphs.
E — For the locals they are a source of great admiration and awe towards their ancestors.
F — This is mainly so due to the lack of artefacts.
G — It appears religious rituals were used for that.
H — But there are hopes machine learning could help in the future.
qs.exp: 'Glyphs generate significant PRIDE and intrigue. (24)______. On the other hand, the script is as much a MYSTERY for them.' → E: For the locals they are a source of GREAT ADMIRATION AND AWE towards their ancestors.

qs.q:
Zipper

"Your suitcase or backpack might spill its contents everywhere (25) ___ it is zipped shut."

A unless
B if
C when
D since
qs.exp: 'Might spill its contents everywhere UNLESS it is zipped shut' — 'unless' = osim ako, ako ne (negiran uvjet).

qs.q:
Zipper

"He was too busy (26) ___ the sewing machine."

A promoting
B to promote
C having promoted
D promote
qs.exp: 'Too busy PROMOTING the sewing machine' — 'too busy + gerund' = preznajut za + gerund.

qs.q:
Zipper

"The product was launched at the World's Fair in Chicago, but it (27) ___ much success."

A won't have
B hasn't had
C hadn't had
D didn't have
qs.exp: 'It DIDN'T HAVE much success' — simple past za prošlu činjenicu (historijski kontekst).

qs.q:
Zipper

"His design increased the number of fastening elements (28) ___ 10 per inch."

A with
B for
C to
D in
qs.exp: 'Increased the number of elements TO 10 per inch' — prijedlog 'to' za dostizanje određene vrijednosti (increase to = povećati na).

qs.q:
Zipper

"But Sundback didn't come up (29) ___ the name!"

A from
B as
C in
D with
qs.exp: 'Didn't come up WITH the name' — frazalni glagol: come up with = smisliti, osmisliti.

qs.q:
Zipper

"It (30) ___ another 20 years before the fashion industry began to use zippers on clothing."

A took
B were
C ran
D passed
qs.exp: 'It TOOK another 20 years before...' — fiksna konstrukcija: it takes (time) = trebati (vremenski period).

qs.q:
Zipper

"This mechanical wonder that has kept our lives 'together' (31) ___ many ways."

A on
B in
C for
D with
qs.exp: 'Kept our lives together IN many ways' — fiksni izraz: in many ways = na mnogo načina.

qs.q:
Zipper

"The zipper was invented by several dedicated inventors, though (32) ___ convinced the general public to accept it in everyday life."

A nor
B none
C never
D neither
qs.exp: 'Though NONE convinced the general public' — 'none' = nitko od njih (none of them).

qs.q:
Brown rice – source of health

"Rice, (33) ______, is not white in its original form."

Odaberi jednu od ponuđenih riječi:
A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'Rice, HOWEVER, is not white in its original form' — 'however' za kontrast (people think rice is white, however...).

qs.q:
Brown rice

"White rice is just brown rice with most of the beneficial nutrients removed and is (34) ______ less healthy."

A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'Most nutrients removed and is THUS less healthy' — 'thus' = dakle, stoga (logical consequence).

qs.q:
Brown rice

"The higher the glycaemic index, the higher the chances of a (35) ______ in blood glucose levels."

A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'Higher chances of a RISE in blood glucose levels' — 'a rise in' = porast u (noun: a rise).

qs.q:
Brown rice

"Raised blood glucose levels (36) ______ to diabetes, so brown rice reduces such risks."

A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'Raised blood glucose levels LEAD to diabetes' — fiksna kolokacija: lead to = dovesti do.

qs.q:
Brown rice

"Brown rice takes longer to digest (37) ______ its high fibre content."

A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'Takes longer to digest DUE TO its high fibre content' — 'due to' + noun = zbog.

qs.q:
Brown rice

"As (38) ______ cuts down the frequency of hunger, gaining excess weight from oily or sugary foods is prevented."

A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'As THIS cuts down the frequency of hunger' — 'this' = fibre (referira se na prethodno navedeno visoko vlakno).

qs.q:
Brown rice

"Studies have found evidence that brown rice may help (39) ______ the health of the heart and the blood vessels."

A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'May help IMPROVE the health of the heart' — 'help + infinitive' = pomoći poboljšati.

qs.q:
Brown rice

"The deficiency of (40) ______ two is associated with heart failure and heart attacks."

A due to / B there / C improve / D however / E rise / F lead / G this / H since / I thus / J these / K arise
qs.exp: 'The deficiency of THESE two (B vitamins and magnesium) is associated with heart failure' — 'these' = zamjenica za prethodno navedena dva elementa.

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that Internet influencers could affect young people in a negative way. Others claim what they do is harmless fun."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA negativan utjecaj: nerealne slike tijela, konzumerizam, loši uzori, anksioznost, cyberbullying. ZA bezopasno: zabava, inspiracija, informacije, kreativnost. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

A — Postman / postwoman
B — IT administrator
C — Travel agent

qs.exp: Prema ključu: 1=H, 2=C, 3=D, 4=A, 5=F.

qs.q:
Food waste — Which person…

A=Alan (checks production/use-by dates before buying; finds distinction between sell-by and use-by confusing; labels often illegible)
B=Ben (food waste = family problem; plan meals; also improve factory/transport standards and reduce CO2)
C=Celine (food waste is major issue; research at university; prosperity + declining prices = less care about surplus; single households)
D=David (food waste = irresponsibility; small shops should cooperate and redistribute surplus to food banks/charities)
E=Eve (deal with problems early; abolish food subsidies → higher prices → more responsibility; angry about landfill data)
F=Fiona (daily: surplus food thrown in wrong bin; higher fines for improper garbage sorting; good laws but ignored)

0. thinks food waste is a major problem of our civilisation? [C=Celine]
1. offers expert opinion on the food waste problem?
2. thinks people should cooperate with local businesses to find the solution?
3. always reads labels on food?
4. is extra careful with the money they spend on food?
5. is concerned about waste disposal?
6. suggests food donation?
7. finds information on food products confusing?
8. thinks household members are responsible for food waste?
9. blames both their neighbours and the local government for food waste?
10. suggests that food should become more expensive?
11. connects the food waste problem to the rich?
12. suggests some legal changes concerning food production?
items: 1 — offers expert opinion on the food waste problem?
2 — thinks people should cooperate with local businesses to find the solution?
4 — is extra careful with the money they spend on food?
7 — finds information on food products confusing?
8 — thinks household members are responsible for food waste?
9 — blames both their neighbours and the local government for food waste?
10 — suggests that food should become more expensive?
11 — connects the food waste problem to the rich?
12 — suggests some legal changes concerning food production?

pairs.l: 1 — offers expert opinion on the food waste problem?
2 — thinks people should cooperate with local businesses to find the solution?
4 — is extra careful with the money they spend on food?
7 — finds information on food products confusing?
8 — thinks household members are responsible for food waste?
9 — blames both their neighbours and the local government for food waste?
10 — suggests that food should become more expensive?
11 — connects the food waste problem to the rich?
12 — suggests some legal changes concerning food production?

qs.exp: 1=C (Celine: 'Having done A LOT OF RESEARCH INTO THE PROBLEM AT UNIVERSITY'). 2=D (David: 'small shops can be ENCOURAGED TO WORK TOGETHER and REDISTRIBUTE the surplus food'). 3=A (Alan: 'CHECKING the production and use-by dates... is what I CONSIDER CRUCIAL... I'm DETERMINED TO DO IT every time'). 4=E (Eve: 'I always THINK TWICE when buying food... because I DESPISE OVERSPENDING'). 5=F (Fiona: 'it is such a big problem for people to SORT OUT BIODEGRADABLE WASTE and put it in the PROPER BIN'). 6=D (David: 'a food bank or a charity that will be more than happy to help'). 7=A (Alan: 'I find it very difficult to make a DISTINCTION between SELL-BY DATE and USE-BY DATE... has to be an expert... BLURRY PRINT'). 8=B (Ben: 'mostly considered a problem at the FAMILY LEVEL: parents buy too much... mothers cook too much... family members eat out'). 9=F (Fiona: 'What I SEE DAILY IN THE APARTMENT BLOCK worries me... the CITY COUNCIL imposed higher fines'). 10=E (Eve: 'abolition of financial subsidies on food. This will result in a RISE IN FOOD PRICES'). 11=C (Celine: 'one of the main drivers is growing PROSPERITY... citizens of the DEVELOPED WORLD care less'). 12=B (Ben: 'establish BETTER STANDARDS IN FACTORIES AND TRANSPORT... REGULATORY MEASURES').

qs.q:
Huntresses of the sea

"She spent her days working at a hair salon. It was a gruelling life: she had trouble finding time to care for her children, she was constantly sick, and interacting with indifferent strangers left her drained. AND, BOTTOM LINE, SHE NEVER SEEMED TO MAKE ENDS MEET."

The main reason Bae left her old job was…
A low income.
B chronic illness.
C human alienation.
D work-life imbalance.
qs.exp: 'BOTTOM LINE, she NEVER SEEMED TO MAKE ENDS MEET' = nije imala dovoljno prihoda = A (low income).

qs.q:
Huntresses of the sea

"Historians say they became EXPERTS IN SUMBISORI: an ancient BREATHING TECHNIQUE, essential in their work, which their MALE COUNTERPARTS COULD NOT MATCH."

According to historians, Jeju women took over the role of free divers because of…
A excessive taxation.
B the shortage of men.
C high seafood demand.
D their mastery of breath.
qs.exp: 'Their male counterparts COULD NOT MATCH' the breathing technique = majstorstvo disanja = D.

qs.q:
Huntresses of the sea

"Bae says she didn't realise before she became a haenyeo that the women take pills to cope with MOTION SICKNESS... She has found this to be the MOST CHALLENGING PART of the job."

According to Bae, the hardest part of doing haenyeo is…
A nausea.
B the high health risk.
C knowing your limits.
D the unpredictable sea.
qs.exp: 'Women take pills to cope with MOTION SICKNESS... she has found this to be the MOST CHALLENGING PART' = mučnina = A.

qs.q:
Huntresses of the sea

"The degradation of the existing UNDERWATER HABITAT has become increasingly severe because LARGE SEAWEED HAS DISAPPEARED, causing MARINE LIFE TO DIE OFF."

At this point, the biggest threat to marine biodiversity in the haenyeo area is…
A water pollution.
B over exploitation.
C habitat destruction.
D invasion of non-native species.
qs.exp: 'DEGRADATION OF THE EXISTING UNDERWATER HABITAT... large seaweed has disappeared... marine life to die off' = uništavanje staništa = C.

qs.q:
Huntresses of the sea

"It is no surprise that it may soon become impossible to find new RECRUITS. Moreover, YOUNG WOMEN ARE LEAVING JEJU and trying to find more stable jobs."

Haenyeo culture is becoming extinct because of…
A migration.
B competition.
C global warming.
D labour conditions.
qs.exp: 'The seas off Korea's southern coast have WARMED' = globalno zatopljenje = C. (Also: young women are leaving, but the KEY says C=global warming as primary cause of the ecological threat.)

qs.q:
Huntresses of the sea

"The Jeju government wants to emphasise the historical importance of the haenyeo, who have been reimagined as KOREA'S PIONEER FEMINISTS, and whose independent income has allowed them to have a VOICE IN THE PREDOMINANTLY PATRIARCHAL FAMILY STRUCTURE."

The government is trying to preserve haenyeo culture because haenyeo divers…
A attract tourists.
B are great role models.
C tackle unemployment.
D safeguard the environment.
qs.exp: 'Korea's PIONEER FEMINISTS... voice in the family structure... democratic community governance and SUSTAINABLE environmental practice' = odlični uzori za feminizam i demokratiju = B.

qs.q:
Tomorrow's cars

"Electric was the first phenomenon to transform cars. (19) ____. However, electric cars are now emerging as a must-have in all market segments because they have many technological advantages."

A Tomorrow's cars will be able to do without their drivers.
B To sum up, the car of the future will be electric, autonomous and connected.
C Tomorrow's factories will be nothing like they are today.
D When it was first introduced, experts envisaged a specific use – for electric public transport for example.
E Such technology is quickly catching up on the autonomous car.
F But also, to ensure connectivity, numerous smart devices will have to be connected and integrated.
G Eventually, through sensors, it will be able to communicate with other vehicles and with the infrastructure.
H The car of the future is still too expensive for ordinary people.
opts: A — Tomorrow's cars will be able to do without their drivers.
B — To sum up, the car of the future will be electric, autonomous and connected.
C — Tomorrow's factories will be nothing like they are today.
D — When it was first introduced, experts envisaged a specific use – for electric public transport for example.
E — Such technology is quickly catching up on the autonomous car.
F — Numerous smart devices will have to be connected and integrated.
G — Eventually it will be able to communicate with other vehicles and the infrastructure.
H — The car of the future is still too expensive for ordinary people.
qs.exp: 'Electric was the FIRST to transform cars. (19)____. HOWEVER, electric cars are now emerging as a MUST-HAVE in all market segments.' → D: When it was FIRST INTRODUCED, experts envisaged a SPECIFIC USE – for electric PUBLIC TRANSPORT for example.

qs.q:
Why are fairy tales important?

"One of the main reasons why fairy tales are important is that they help in a child's character (25) ___."

A evolution
B advancement
C progress
D development
qs.exp: 'Character DEVELOPMENT' — fiksna kolokacija: character development = razvoj karaktera/ličnosti.

qs.q:
Why are fairy tales important?

"We still remember the fantastic characters such as kings, fairies and princesses who (26) ___ our life from an early age."

A are influencing
B have influenced
C had to influence
D should influence
qs.exp: 'Characters who HAVE INFLUENCED our life from an early age' — present perfect za trajan utjecaj koji seže do sadašnjosti.

qs.q:
Why are fairy tales important?

"They may be dangerous in (27) ____ of hidden messages."

A terms
B spite
C charge
D favour
qs.exp: 'Dangerous in TERMS OF hidden messages' — fiksni izraz: in terms of = u pogledu, što se tiče.

qs.q:
Why are fairy tales important?

"Original fairy tales were not (28) ____ for children."

A expected
B given
C meant
D aimed

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some say that one hundred years ago people lived a healthier life. Others say that the quality of life has never been better."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA bolji život 100 godina: čistiji zrak/voda, prirodna hrana, više tjelovježbe, manje stresa, jača zajednica. ZA bolji sadašnji život: medicina, dugotrajalnost, udobnost, pristup hrani/obrazovanju. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

the zoo earns 1.5 million pounds from its visitors annually.
closing the zoo would save more money from the budget for conservation.
part of the money earned from visitors goes to conservation work in the field.

"Relocating to a country where your language of choice is spoken is without (30) ___ the best way to learn."

A fear
B doubt
C difficulty
D suspicion
qs.exp: 'Without DOUBT the best way to learn' — fiksni izraz: without doubt = nedvojbeno, nesumnjivo.

qs.q:
Learning a foreign language

"If you only ever (31) ___ with another language learner, you'll both find yourselves stuck on a plateau."

A practise
B will practise
C would practise
D had practised
qs.exp: 'If you only ever PRACTISE with another language learner' — conditional 1: if + present simple → will. 'Practise' = present simple.

qs.q:
Learning a foreign language

"When you (32) ___ the time to find a native speaker, you'll find yourself progressing much more quickly."

A set
B keep
C take
D save

qs.q:
Being mindful

Odaberi jednu od ponuđenih riječi:
A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less
qs.exp: 'Increasing your capacity FOR mindfulness' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: capacity for = kapacitet za.

qs.q:
Being mindful

A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less

qs.q:
Being mindful

"(35) ____ focusing on the here and now, many people who practise mindfulness find that they are less likely to get caught up in worries."

A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less

qs.q:
Being mindful

"They are (36) ____ preoccupied with concerns about success and self-esteem."

A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less
qs.exp: 'They are LESS preoccupied with concerns about success' — 'less' = manje (komparativ malo).

qs.q:
Being mindful

"As (37) ____ greater well-being isn't enough of an incentive, scientists have discovered that mindfulness techniques help improve physical health."

A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less
qs.exp: 'As IF greater well-being isn't enough of an incentive' — fiksni izraz: as if = kao da (implies it IS enough but they're adding more).

qs.q:
Being mindful

"There is more (38) ____ one way to practise mindfulness."

A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less
qs.exp: 'There is more THAN one way to practise mindfulness' — komparativna konstrukcija: more than = više od.

qs.q:
Being mindful

"The goal is to achieve a state of focused alertness by deliberately paying attention to the (39) ___ we base our judgements on."

A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less

qs.q:
Being mindful

"One can cultivate mindfulness by directing attention to moment-to-moment (40) ___ during everyday activities."

A than / B thoughts / C from / D for / E by / F up / G with / H if / I that / J sensations / K less

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that environmental damage is the price we pay for human progress. Others say human progress is possible without harming the environment."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA ekološku štetu kao cijenu: industrijski razvoj, rast populacije, globalizacija, teško izbjeći. ZA razvoj bez štete: obnovljiva energija, zelene tehnologije, cirkularna ekonomija, promjene u ponašanju. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:
You will hear five people talking about going to the gym.
Match each speaker (1–5) with one option from A–H.
Do not use any letter more than once. There are three options you do not need.

What is each person's reason for going to the gym?
A — To build up muscles.
B — To become a personal trainer.
C — To lose weight.
D — To get rid of stress.
E — To recover after an injury.
F — To compete in high-level sporting events.
G — To improve their social life.
H — To feel better about themselves.
rights: B — To become a personal trainer.
D — To get rid of stress.
E — To recover after an injury.
F — To compete in high-level sporting events.
G — To improve their social life.
H — To feel better about themselves.

pairs.r: D — To get rid of stress.
H — To feel better about themselves.
G — To improve their social life.
B — To become a personal trainer.
F — To compete in high-level sporting events.

qs.exp: Prema ključu: 1=D, 2=H, 3=G, 4=B, 5=F.

qs.q:
Holidays — Which person…
