It's a WIN-WIN situation'). 5=C (Colin: 'I DIDN'T EXPECT TO HAVE SO MANY SHOTS to be honest' = cjepiva). 6=A (Alison: 'Considering the facilities and locations, it's REALLY QUITE REASONABLE'). 7=F (Frances: 'although the CLIMBING WILL BE QUITE DEMANDING... fingers crossed'). 8=B (Ben: 'it was a SNAP DECISION in the end'). 9=D (Deborah: 'the good old CANAL BARGE' = brodica). 10=A (Alison: 'I'm anticipating there'll be some THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS from this trip'). 11=D (Deborah: 'you OVERNIGHT AT PUBS OR MARINAS ALONG THE WAY'). 12=B (Ben: 'I hope getting SUPPLIES won't be a HEADACHE' = self-catering).

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"As students of architecture we used to refer to trees as GRACEFUL SUPPLEMENTS MAKING A HOUSE FEEL LIKE A HOME and ENRICHING THE VIEW FROM THE WINDOW."

Which statement about trees reflects Tom Baker's initial professional interest in trees?
A They remove CO2 from the atmosphere.
B They bring songbirds and wildlife close by.
C They make a neighbourhood more beautiful.
D They reduce the heat from streets and buildings.
opts: They remove CO2 from the atmosphere.
They bring songbirds and wildlife close by.
They make a neighbourhood more beautiful.
They reduce the heat from streets and buildings.
qs.exp: 'As students of ARCHITECTURE we used to refer to trees as GRACEFUL SUPPLEMENTS MAKING A HOUSE FEEL LIKE A HOME' = čine susjedstvo ljepšim = C.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"After a local opinion poll, another interpretation has emerged, DEFINING THEM AS PLACES WHERE PEOPLE CAN INTERACT."

What are the benefits of more parks and green spaces, according to Brookson's residents?
A They reduce social isolation.
B They lower their carbon footprint.
C They produce habitats for many species.
D They present more opportunities for exercise.
opts: They produce habitats for many species.
They present more opportunities for exercise.
qs.exp: 'Local opinion poll: defining them as places WHERE PEOPLE CAN INTERACT' = smanjuju socijalnu izolaciju = A.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"City planners may PRIORITISE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND INFRASTRUCTURE OVER GREEN SPACES... especially in HIGHLY URBANISED AREAS WHERE THERE IS LITTLE ROOM for property development."

Why are green spaces often not included in city planning?
A Because of the cities' low housing budgets.
B Because humans have changed them beyond return.
C Because people fail to realise how important green spaces are.
D Because in congested parts of the city space is in high demand.
opts: Because of the cities' low housing budgets.
Because humans have changed them beyond return.
Because people fail to realise how important green spaces are.
Because in congested parts of the city space is in high demand.
qs.exp: 'Highly urbanised areas where there is LITTLE ROOM for property development' = prostor je tražen u prenapučenim dijelovima = D.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"We're currently promoting the latest data referring to the REDUCTION OF STRESS LEVELS AND ANXIETY."

Which slogan would summarise Tom's most recent campaign for making green spaces more popular?
A Green spaces remove pollutants.
B Green spaces improve mental health.
C Green spaces are educational and fun.
D Green spaces develop the identity of cities.
opts: Green spaces are educational and fun.
Green spaces develop the identity of cities.
qs.exp: 'Currently promoting the latest data referring to the REDUCTION OF STRESS LEVELS AND ANXIETY' = zeleni prostori poboljšavaju mentalno zdravlje = B.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"A solution may be creating MINI FORESTS IN THE SMALLER SPACES, growing up to 30 TIMES AS FAST as conventional ones."

How can green spaces be developed in urban areas?
A By employing rapid-growth techniques.
B By removing old buildings to insert green spaces.
C By letting existing green areas and natural forests grow.
D By planting numerous tree species to restore deteriorated land.
opts: By removing old buildings to insert green spaces.
By letting existing green areas and natural forests grow.
By planting numerous tree species to restore deteriorated land.
qs.exp: 'Mini forests growing up to 30 TIMES AS FAST as conventional ones' = tehnikama brzog rasta = A.

qs.q:
Trees and Green Spaces in Cities

"MAINTAINING BIODIVERSITY for any green area is key for its own and HUMAN SURVIVAL in general."

In the last paragraph, what does Tom say should be given priority when planning a green space?
A The opinions and attitudes of the local population.
B The local government's plans for a particular area.
C The provision of habitats for local plant and animal species.
D The reduction of the environmental impact of life in city areas.
opts: The opinions and attitudes of the local population.
The local government's plans for a particular area.
The provision of habitats for local plant and animal species.
The reduction of the environmental impact of life in city areas.
qs.exp: 'MAINTAINING BIODIVERSITY for any green area is KEY for its own and human survival' = osiguravanje staništa za biljke i životinje = C.

qs.q:
Downshifting

"In general, labour markets have become less regulated and more insecure for workers. (19) ____. English has a word for it – 'downshifting' – signifying a career change to an activity perhaps less well paid, but offering better job satisfaction."

A They are less likely to focus on these aspects and more on the notion of job satisfaction.
B The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
D Part of this trend is that professionals are enthusiastically embracing 'trades', as they were once dismissively termed.
E Losing a job can be a shock to the system and have unexpected results.
F Many respondents reported being put off by the idea of a lifetime spent at a desk interacting with a computer screen.
G There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
opts: A — They are less likely to focus on these aspects and more on the notion of job satisfaction.
B — The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C — That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
E — Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F — Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G — There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H — This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
qs.exp: 'Labour markets have become LESS REGULATED AND MORE INSECURE for workers. (19)____. English has a word for it – DOWNSHIFTING.' → D: Part of this trend is that professionals are enthusiastically EMBRACING 'TRADES', as they were once dismissively termed.

qs.q:
Downshifting

"Millennials and younger generations must increasingly make do with jobs less prestigious than their parents' or for which they are overqualified. (20) ____. What are we to make, therefore, of the manager who actively wants to become a cheese maker?"

A They are less likely to focus on these aspects.
B The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
D Professionals are enthusiastically embracing 'trades'.
E Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
opts: A — They are less likely to focus on these aspects.
B — The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C — That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
E — Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F — Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G — There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H — This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
qs.exp: Greška u ključu — Q20=H je već korišten za Q19. Ispravan odgovor za Q20 (prema kontekstu) je H (already used) → Prema ključu 20=H označava: This is characterised as unfortunate, unfair imposition (primjenjuje se na Millenials making do with less prestige). ALI ključ kaže 20=H što bi bio duplikat Q19. Gledam ključ koji jasno kaže 19=D i 20=H. Dakle Q19=D i Q20=H.

Downshifting

B The work has immediacy and tangible results.

E Losing a job can be a shock to the system.

B — The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C — That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
E — Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F — Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G — There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H — This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
qs.exp: 'Prize fulfilment over material reward. (21)____. SOME ACCESS BENEFITS during retraining; others have income from family or savings to FALL BACK ON.' → C: THAT SAID, they often have the reassurance of a SAFETY NET.

qs.q:
Downshifting

"The new career may not offer the kudos, social opportunities or financial reward they might otherwise expect, but the experiential perspective results in a change in expectation. (22) ____. As a result, they rarely feel a loss of status."

A They are less likely to focus on these aspects and more on the notion of job satisfaction.
B The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
D Professionals are enthusiastically embracing 'trades'.
E Losing a job can be a shock to the system.

opts: A — They are less likely to focus on these aspects and more on the notion of job satisfaction.
B — The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C — That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
E — Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F — Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G — There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H — This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
qs.exp: 'The experiential perspective results in a change in expectation. (22)____. They RARELY FEEL A LOSS OF STATUS.' → A: They are LESS LIKELY TO FOCUS ON THESE ASPECTS (kudos, financial reward) and MORE ON THE NOTION OF JOB SATISFACTION.

qs.q:
Downshifting

"This brings us to the second major conclusion of the study, which has more to do with the nature of the employment being abandoned. (23) ____. This is manifested in rejection of an unhealthy sedentary existence, as well as the narrow focus of stratified work in a large faceless company."

A They are less likely to focus on these aspects.
B The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
D Professionals are enthusiastically embracing 'trades'.
E Losing a job can be a shock to the system.

opts: A — They are less likely to focus on these aspects.
B — The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C — That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
E — Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F — Many respondents reported being put off by the idea of a lifetime at a desk interacting with a computer screen.
G — There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H — This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.

qs.q:
Downshifting

"In stark contrast, manual activity offers the gratification of physical involvement. There are perceived benefits to mind and body. (24) ____. This is completely in opposition to the soul-destroying tedium of a corporate culture."

A They are less likely to focus on these aspects.
B The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
D Professionals are enthusiastically embracing 'trades'.
E Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
opts: A — They are less likely to focus on these aspects.
B — The work has immediacy and tangible results.
C — That said, they often have the reassurance of a safety net.
E — Losing a job can be a shock to the system.
F — Many respondents reported being put off by a lifetime at a desk.
G — There is a measurable increase in spirituality.
H — This is characterised as an unfortunate, even unfair, imposition.
qs.exp: 'Manual activity offers gratification of physical involvement. Benefits to mind and body. (24)____. This is in OPPOSITION to the soul-destroying TEDIUM of corporate culture.' → B: The work has IMMEDIACY AND TANGIBLE RESULTS.

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"The way someone talks (25) ____ to their identity."

A contrasts
B consents
C contributes
D concurs
qs.exp: 'The way someone talks CONTRIBUTES to their identity' — fiksna kolokacija: contribute to = doprinositi, biti dio.

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"Why is it that some people lose their regional or national accent, (26) ____ for others it remains firmly in place?"

A as
B while
C maybe
D again
qs.exp: 'Some people lose their accent, WHILE for others it remains in place' — 'while' za kontrast između dviju situacija.

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"Research shows that the need to conform may alter our vocal production, (27) ____ we like it or not."

A whether
B although
C unless
D as
qs.exp: 'WHETHER we like it or not' — fiksni izraz: whether... or not = bez obzira na to.

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"The way (28) ____ which they speak may be of less importance to their sense of identity."

A by
B of
C on
D in
qs.exp: 'The way IN WHICH they speak' — fiksna konstrukcija: the way in which = način na koji.

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"As we encounter wider societal groupings this same instinct to assimilate (29) ____ us to modify our speech patterns accordingly."

A would cause
B might cause
C must have caused
D could have been causing
qs.exp: 'This same instinct MIGHT CAUSE us to modify our speech patterns' — 'might' za mogućnost (nije nužno, ali može se dogoditi).

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"There are others (30) ____ voices remain impervious to change."

A who's
B where
C which
D whose
qs.exp: 'There are others WHOSE voices remain impervious to change' — genitiv relativna zamjenica 'whose' (čiji glasovi).

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"In addition, (31) ____ a person possess the accent of what is deemed to be a prestigious group in society, they will consequently feel less pressure to abandon that advantage."

A could
B shall
C should
D would
qs.exp: 'SHOULD a person possess the accent of a prestigious group' — 'should' u kondicionalu (formalni uvjet = if a person should possess).

qs.q:
Losing an Accent

"They will consequently feel (32) ____ pressure to abandon that advantage."

A low
B high
C less
D more
qs.exp: 'Feel LESS pressure to abandon that advantage' — 'less' = manje pritiska (ako imaš prestižan naglasak, imaš MANJE razloga da ga napustiš).

qs.q:
The Future with ChatGPT

"It is a GPT model that (33) ___ deep learning techniques to generate human-like text."

Odaberi jednu od ponuđenih riječi:
A proposes / B does / C there / D raises / E their / F to / G its / H uses / I about / J for / K by / L those / M makes
qs.exp: 'A GPT model that USES deep learning techniques' — 'uses' = koristi (kolokacija: use techniques).

qs.q:
The Future with ChatGPT

"ChatGPT answers users' requests without credits or reference (34) ___ where the information comes from."

A proposes / B does / C there / D raises / E their / F to / G its / H uses / I about / J for / K by / L those / M makes
qs.exp: 'Without credits or reference TO where the information comes from' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: reference to = referenca na.

qs.q:
The Future with ChatGPT

"...which poses a huge copyright problem, particularly because of ChatGPT's widespread usage (35) ___ students."

A proposes / B does / C there / D raises / E their / F to / G its / H uses / I about / J for / K by / L those / M makes
qs.exp: 'Widespread usage BY students' — 'by' za počinitelja/korisnika (usage by students = korištenje od strane studenata).

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people believe the Internet is a reliable source of healthcare information. Others claim it cannot replace a visit to the doctor."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA internet: brz pristup, šire znanje, korisno za manje simptome, samoobrazovanje, dostupnost. ZA posjetu liječniku: profesionalna dijagnoza, fizički pregled, personalizirana njega, opasnost od pogrešnih informacija. Vlastito mišljenje.

qs.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.

qs.q:

qs.q:
Learning Foreign Languages — Which person…

A=Alan (communicative learner; ignores structure; speaks regardless of mistakes; thanked shop assistant for correcting pronunciation)
B=Ben (friend advised memorising 50 words; compiled script of useful phrases; language-immersion meet-up group; needs to focus on grammar in future)

D=David (B2 in Italian but can't speak to native speakers; instructors only taught vocab from bilingual lists; recalling in real-life is tough)
E=Eve (keen traveller; volunteered worldwide; picked up basics in several languages; singing improved pronunciation; mastered idioms)
F=Fiona (native speakers consider her gifted; records herself speaking; listens back; replaces familiar words with synonyms; checks progress)

0. is an auditory learner? [E=Eve]
1. believes that determination, formal education and practice lead to success?
2. has difficulty when speaking the language?
3. uses a wide range of activities to get exposed to the new language?
4. is particularly interested in expanding vocabulary?
5. is entirely self-taught?
6. doesn't worry about making mistakes?
7. is aware of multiple connotations of words?
8. likes to get feedback from native speakers?
9. has gradually improved their reading skill?
10. blames the teaching methods for lack of language competence?
11. plans to upgrade their grammar?
12. learns through images?
items: 1 — believes that determination, formal education and practice lead to success?
2 — has difficulty when speaking the language?
3 — uses a wide range of activities to get exposed to the new language?
4 — is particularly interested in expanding vocabulary?
7 — is aware of multiple connotations of words?
8 — likes to get feedback from native speakers?
9 — has gradually improved their reading skill?
10 — blames the teaching methods for lack of language competence?

pairs.l: 1 — believes that determination, formal education and practice lead to success?
2 — has difficulty when speaking the language?
3 — uses a wide range of activities to get exposed to the new language?
4 — is particularly interested in expanding vocabulary?
7 — is aware of multiple connotations of words?
8 — likes to get feedback from native speakers?
9 — has gradually improved their reading skill?
10 — blames the teaching methods for lack of language competence?

qs.exp: 1=F (Fiona: 'talent is nothing without CONSISTENT HARD WORK and EXPERT TEACHERS'). 2=D (David: 'I am RELUCTANT to engage in any VERBAL EXCHANGE with native speakers'). 3=B (Ben: 'memorising words... compiled a script... language-immersion meet-up group... absorb it in MANY WAYS'). 4=F (Fiona: replaces familiar words with synonyms = expanding vocabulary). 5=E (Eve: volunteered worldwide, 'PICK UP SOME BASICS' without formal teaching). 6=A (Alan: 'I will use it REGARDLESS OF THE RISK of using some awkward or incorrect word'). 7=E (Eve: 'memorise the SUBTLE DIFFERENCES IN THE MEANING AND PRONUNCIATION of words'). 8=A (Alan: 'I THANKED THE SHOP ASSISTANT FOR CORRECTING MY PRONUNCIATION'). 9=C (Celine: 'I UNDERSTAND MORE WITH EACH CHAPTER and need to LOOK UP FEWER WORDS'). 10=D (David: 'instructors would teach us vocabulary and WRITE ENDLESS BILINGUAL LISTS... RECALLING A WORD IN A REAL-LIFE CONTEXT IS STILL A TOUGH CHALLENGE'). 11=B (Ben: 'I will have to FOCUS ON STRUCTURES AND TENSES in the future'). 12=C (Celine: 'my brain can easily memorise new language structures via THE PICTURES').

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

qs.q:
Crop Circles – Messages in the Fields

"Elaborate motifs, often tens of metres across... 'Crop circles' were CONCENTRATED IN AREAS OF ENGLAND CLOSE TO ANCIENT ARCHAEOLOGICAL SITES like Stonehenge and the Avebury Stone Circle."

The crop circles were known to be…
A the work of alien cultures.
B arranged in complex patterns.
C at sites of archaeological interest.
D made by farmers seeking publicity.
qs.exp: 'ENORMOUS, ELABORATE MOTIFS, often tens of metres across' = složeni uzorci = B.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"Although the crops would ALWAYS SPRING BACK INTACT to their previous position."

One thing that the crop circles did NOT cause was…
A physical damage to plants.
B an increase in legal consultations.
C an upsurge of interest in unidentified flying objects.
D confrontations between landowners and unwelcome visitors.
opts: an upsurge of interest in unidentified flying objects.
confrontations between landowners and unwelcome visitors.
qs.exp: 'The crops would ALWAYS SPRING BACK INTACT' = nije bilo fizičke štete biljkama = A.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"The mystery about their origins provided THE IDEAL OPPORTUNITY FOR NEWSPAPER EDITORS. They SEIZED ON THE REGULAR OPPORTUNITIES for writing extensive articles featuring stunning aerial photographs."

According to the author, those who benefited most from crop circles were…
A local people.
B new-age travellers.
C newspaper editors.
D Doug Bower and Dave Chorley.
qs.exp: 'The ideal opportunity for NEWSPAPER EDITORS. They seized on the regular opportunities for writing extensive articles' = novinari imali najviše koristi = C.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"Fields of wheat and corn had become ARENAS OF CONFLICT during the historic miners' strike... there were VIOLENT CONFRONTATIONS BETWEEN POLICE AND NEW-AGE TRAVELLERS... the RAVE CULTURE of pop-up open-air dance parties was getting under way."

The author draws particular attention to fields as…
A sites of particular historic interest.
B places inhabited by sun-worshippers.
C significant, in the broader sense, to agriculture.
D places characterised by frequent public disturbances.
opts: significant, in the broader sense, to agriculture.
places characterised by frequent public disturbances.
qs.exp: 'Arenas of CONFLICT during the miners' strike... VIOLENT CONFRONTATIONS between police... RAVE CULTURE' = mjesta čestih javnih nemira = D.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"These cheeky exploits... were eccentric expressions of RESISTANCE to the increasing concentration of English land in the hands of financiers... can be seen as A FURTHER BLOSSOMING OF LAND-BASED ART by practitioners ranging from Andy Goldsworthy to Banksy."

The article describes crop circles as…
A saying nothing at all.
B keeping a pact of secrecy.
C focusing attention on investments.
D extending the repertoire of artistic expression.
opts: extending the repertoire of artistic expression.
qs.exp: 'A FURTHER BLOSSOMING OF LAND-BASED ART' = proširenje repertoara umjetničkog izražaja = D.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"It COULD NEVER BE MONETISED, and this is why... what remains is simply a TRADITION OF GREAT ART."

According to the author, it was impossible to exploit crop circles because they…
A were not permanent.
B could not be exhibited.
C were made anonymously.
D were associated with the rave culture.
opts: were associated with the rave culture.
qs.exp: 'It could never be MONETISED... their VERY SHORT-LIVED WORK' = nije trajno = A.

qs.q:

A Like any new positive behaviour that you undertake, they take time and practice.
B When we are focused on the present moment, we are not contemplating the past or worrying about the future.
C Exercise, take part in a conversation, watch a show you love, or work on another project.
D This can negatively impact our mood and, ultimately, how we work.
E If it is still a concern, then you can proceed to problem solving.
F Acknowledge the negative aspects and then evaluate if there are other ways to think about it.
G It results in us making assumptions about what was meant by their comment, or reading between the lines.
H Instead of asking why something happened, ask if there is an answer to the problem.

C either

qs.exp: 'Dogs NOT ONLY process the meaning of words BUT ALSO pick up on the emotional tone' — korelativna konstrukcija: not only... but also.

How Dogs Understand Us

A adept
B keen
C prone
D ready
qs.exp: 'Dogs are ADEPT AT understanding non-verbal cues' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: adept at = vješt u.

How Dogs Understand Us

A by
B in
C to
D with

How Dogs Understand Us

A dealt
B taken
C talked
D seen

How Dogs Understand Us

A continues

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"Intuitive design, (33) ___, is often used informally to describe designs that are easy to use."

Odaberi jednu od ponuđenih riječi:
A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'Intuitive design, HOWEVER, is often used informally to describe designs that are easy to use' — 'however' za kontrast (experts can't agree on a definition, however it is often used informally).

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"When a user is able to understand and use a design (34) ___, or rather, without consciously thinking about how to do it, we describe the design as 'intuitive'."

A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'A user is able to understand and use a design IMMEDIATELY, or rather, without consciously thinking' — 'immediately' = odmah (bez svjesnog razmišljanja).

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"While there is (35) ___ standard definition, some research groups have worked towards building a clearer understanding."

A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'While there is NO standard definition' — 'no' za negiranje imenice (nema standardne definicije).

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"Some research groups (36) ___ worked towards building a clearer understanding of the term 'intuitive design'."

A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'Some research groups HAVE WORKED towards building a clearer understanding' — present perfect: have + past participle.

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"Members of the interdisciplinary research group Intuitive Use of User Interfaces (37) ___ that intuition is not a feature of design."

A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'Members ARGUE that intuition is not a feature of design' — 'argue' = tvrditi, zauzeti stav (akademski glagol za iznošenje argumenta).

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"So, if we want to (38) ___ how intuitive a design is, we must also take into consideration who will use the design."

A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'If we want to EVALUATE how intuitive a design is' — 'evaluate' = procijeniti, vrednovati.

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"Users will feel that a design is intuitive when it is based on principles from some (39) ___ domains that are well known to them."

A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'Based on principles from some OTHER domains that are well known to them' — 'other' = neki drugi (domeni).

qs.q:
What Is Intuitive Design?

"This is particularly relevant in today's highly dynamic digital environment where consumers (40) ___ that they have instant access to whatever they need."

A evaluate / B demand / C argue / D have / E had / F only / G such / H other / I however / J especially / K immediately / L moreover / M no
qs.exp: 'Consumers DEMAND that they have instant access to whatever they need' — 'demand' = zahtijevati (potrošači zahtijevaju trenutni pristup).

qs.q:
Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people say that the gap between younger and older generations is getting bigger. Others say the differences are disappearing."
